ओल्ड कोर्टहाउस स्क्वायर के पश्चिम दिस सोनोमा काउंटी समुदाय के सदस्य सब हाथ स लिखल समर्थन के चिन्ह आ नेपाली झंडा ल क जमा भ गेल छल। उपस्थित लोकनि “नेपाल लेल प्रार्थना करू” शब्दक वर्तनी आ देशक लाल, उज्जर आ नील रंगक दू नुकीला झंडाक रूपरेखा बनेबाक लेल मोमबत्तीक व्यवस्था केलनि ।

इंडिया टुडे के अनुसार, 5 सितम्बर, 2026 तक,1,344 लोगऽ के मौत के पुष्टि होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ 5,000 स॑ भी अधिक लोग अखनी तलक लापता छै, तिब्बत म॑ 21 लोगऽ के मौत के खबर छै आरू 500 स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता छै, आरू 13,000 स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ क॑ बाढ़ स॑ सफलतापूर्वक बचालऽ गेलऽ छै ।

एसआरजेसी क कंप्यूटर साइंस क छात्र कियान केसी अपन मां क संग जागरण मे शामिल भेलाह। विपत्ति भेलाक बादसँ नेपालमे मित्र-परिवारक सम्पर्क नहि भऽ सकल अछि ।

कियान केसी कहलकै, “बरखा एखनो चलि रहल अछि;हमरा हुनका लोकनिक कोनो जवाब नहि भेटल अछि, आ ने हुनकर परिवार सँ.” “हम हुनकर बहिन, हुनकर पितियौत भाइ, हुनकर अपन परिवार’क सदस्य केँ मेसेज करबाक प्रयास केने छी;हुनका दिस सँ कोनो जवाब नहि.”

फॉल सेमेस्टर शुरू भेला स कियान केसी कहला जे ओ अपन स्कूल क काज जल्दी पूरा करबा लेल काज केलथि ताकि ओ नेपाल मे जरूरत पर ध्यान द सकथि। ओ अपना कए स्थिति स अपडेट करैत रहलाह, अपन इंस्टाग्राम पेज पर जानकारी साझा करैत रहलाह, दान दैत रहलाह आ प्रार्थना करैत रहलाह।

एसआरजेसी कम्प्यूटर साइंस के छात्र क्यान केसी के आश्चर्य छै कि 1 सितम्बर 2026 के सांता रोजा के ओआईडी कोर्टहाउस स्क्वायर में नेपाल के लेल शोक आ मोमबत्ती के इजोत के दौरान हुनकर परिवार आ मित्र सुरक्षित छैथ कि नै।(पैसिफिक जेरेमी)

सोनोमा काउंटी के तीन मेयर एहि आयोजन के आयोजन करय वाला समूह कैलिफोर्निया के संयुक्त नेपाली के आमंत्रण पर जागरण में भाग लेलखिन्ह. सांता रोजा के मार्क स्टेप, विंडसर के रोजा रेनोजा, आ रोहनेर्ट पार्क के एमिली सैनबर्न।

सैनबर्न, “आई हार्ट रोहनेर्ट पार्क” स्वेटशर्ट पहिरने कहलनि, "हमरा सभक सिटी ऑफ रोहनेर्ट पार्क के माध्यम सं एकटा फाउंडेशन अछि. तें हम सब हर दोसर साल गैर-लाभकारी संगठन लेल अनुदान करैत छी जाबत धरि ओ समुदाय के फायदा पहुंचेबाक लेल किछु क' रहल छथि, आ तें हम ई सुनिश्चित करय चाहैत छी जे यूएनसी एहि सालक अंत मे जखन खुजत तखन ओहि अनुदान लेल आवेदन क' रहल अछि."

दोहरी नामांकित एसआरजेसी आरू सांता रोजा हाई स्कूल केरऽ छात्र जे अपनऽ अंतिम नाम बिप्लोव्वाग्ले स॑ पहचान करलकै, न॑ ई आयोजन केरऽ बहुत हिस्सा चंदा इकट्ठा करै म॑ बिताय देलकै । ओ भीड़ मे दान देबाक महत्व व्यक्त करैत बतौलनि जे एहि मे 5 अरब डॉलर सं बेसी के नुकसान अछि जे नेपाल के वार्षिक सकल घरेलू उत्पाद के लगभग दसवां हिस्सा अछि.

जुटाओल गेल धनराशि नेपाल सरकारक प्रधानमन्त्री आपदा राहत कोषमे पठाओल जाएत ।

नेपाल सरकार केरऽ आधिकारिक वेबसाइट स॑ आपदा राहत केरऽ अपील म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि “ नेपाल सरकार न॑ प्रधानमंत्री केरऽ प्राकृतिक आपदा राहत कोष आरू प्रधानमंत्री राहत कोष क॑ प्रधानमंत्री आरू मंत्री परिषद केरऽ कार्यालय म॑ आर्थिक सहयोग दै लेली सब नागरिक, संगठन, आरू संस्था स॑ ईमानदारी स॑ अपील करै छै ।

प्रधानमन्त्री आपदा राहत कोषके लेल नगद चन्दा संकलनके लेल स्थानीय नेपाली स्वामित्वके व्यवसायमे चंदा डिब्बा लगाओल जाएत युएनसीके मनोज थाउगुन्ना बतौलनि । थौगुन्ना न॑ द ओक लीफ क॑ उपलब्ध कराय देलऽ गेलऽ एगो सूची के अनुसार दान बॉक्स केरऽ स्थानऽ म॑ सांता रोजा म॑ दरबार किचन इंडियन एंड नेपाली कुजिन आरू नीलमेड फार्मास्यूटिकल्स, रोहनेर्ट पार्क म॑ काठमांडू स्मोक शॉप आरू वेस्ट कोस्ट सॉरडो, आरू नोवाटो म॑ बाटिका इंडियन बिस्ट्रो शामिल छै ।

यूएनसी के अध्यक्ष दीपक तिमसिना नँ कहलकै कि ई जागरण महिला सिनी लेली पहलें स॑ निर्धारित हरितालिका महोत्सव के जगह लेलकै जेकरा मूल रूप स॑ वेटरन मेमोरियल बिल्डिंग म॑ आयोजित करलऽ जाय के योजना छेलै ।

“नेपाल मे भेल विनाशकारी बाढ़ि आ प्राकृतिक आपदाक आलोक मे, जाहि सँ हमर साथी नेपाली लोकनिक जान-माल, संपत्ति, आ अपार कष्टक काफी नुकसान भेल अछि, हम सब गहींर दुखी आ हृदयविदारक छी,” यूएनसी तीज रद्द करबाक सूचना मे कहलक अछि । “एहि समय मे जखन नेपाल मे हमर बहुत रास भाई, बहिन, परिवार आ समुदाय एहन पीड़ा आ कष्ट क सामना क रहल अछि, हमरा सब कए लगैत अछि जे अपन पावनि रोजाना क तरह मनब उचित नहि होएत।”

नॉर्थ बे केरऽ एशियाई अमेरिकन पैसिफिक आइलैंडर कोलिशन केरऽ अध्यक्ष आरू उपाध्यक्ष लॉरी फोंग आरू ग्रेस चेउंग-शुलमैन न॑ शुरू म॑ तीज समारोह म॑ भाग लेबै के योजना बनयने छेलै, लेकिन एकरऽ बदला म॑ जागरण म॑ भाग लेलकै ।

समारोह शुरू होबय सं पहिने फोंग कहलनि जे, ई सबटा मानवता के बात अछि, आ जौं हम सब सचमुच अपन मानवता के पैर आगू राखब त हम सब जुड़ल छी। ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाली समुदाय एहि क्षेत्र मे तेजी सँ बढ़य बला जातीय समूह मे सँ एक अछि।

1 सितम्बर 2026 के सांता रोजा के ओआईडी कोर्टहाउस स्क्वायर पर नेपाल के लेल शोक आ मोमबत्ती के इजोत के आयोजन के दौरान नेपाल में 26 अगस्त के आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के पीड़ित सब के संग एकजुटता में ठाढ़ छथि।(पैसिफिक जेरेमी)

मंगलवार कए जागरण स पहिने रुक सुंदरमूर्धी कहला जे भारत स बहुत लोक तीर्थ क रूप मे मनसरोवर जाइत छथि, ताहि लेल ओतय सेहो बहुत रास भारतीय लोक लापता भ गेल छथि।

सुंदरमूर्धी पेटालुमा में स्थित नॉर्थ बे हिन्दू सेंटर के सदस्य छैथ। ओ बतौलनि जे नेपाल मे प्रभावित क्षेत्र भारत आ तिब्बतक दू टा महत्वपूर्ण तीर्थस्थल के बीच अछि ।

सुंदरमूर्धी हिन्दू तीर्थ स्थल कैलाश पर्वत आ मनसरोवर झील क बारे मे कहला जे जीवन मे एक बेर सब कए ओ तीर्थ यात्रा करबा लेल जेबाक अछि।

अनिश्चितताक बादो उपस्थित लोकनि आशावादी रहलाह । सुमन घिमिरे एखनो लापता लोकक बारे मे कहलनि जे, एखन ओ सब गायब अछि, ताहि लेल कोनो मृत शरीर नहि भेटल अछि आ ने किछु, मुदा किछु आशा अछि, जा धरि लाश मृत नहि भेटैत अछि ता धरि लोक के किछु आशा रहैत अछि।

full_article:
Two people were rescued in separate operations on Saturday as Nepal continues dealing with the fallout from devastating floods that hit the country 10 days ago.

The Nepali military said Saturday a team made up of its army and South Korean disaster experts saved a Chinese man from a 740 foot tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, The Guardian reported. CNN wrote that a 60-year-old Nepali woman was found downriver in a four-story building in Betrawati.

A local official said the family of the woman, Chandika Shrestha, started ceremonial last rites and preparations for her funeral, as they thought she died, according to CNN.

Authorities said at least 1,362 people died due to the flooding. Around 900 hydropower workers at facilities near the Trishuli River are among the thousands of missing.

On Friday, rescuers pulled two workers, a mechanical foreman and a supervisor, alive from a tunnel in the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant. Both were reportedly in stable condition, and taken to a hospital in Kathmandu for treatment.

Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha, the head of the Nepal Electricity Authority, said that a third man’s body was recovered at the hydropower plant, too, The New York Times wrote. The man was a mechanical engineer, he said.

Rescuers said they heard voices from inside the tunnel on Friday morning, which helped them locate the workers. More voices can still be heard inside, the rescuers said.

The flash floods and mudslides began after a glacial collapse near the Nepal–China border on Aug. 26.

Nepal’s Foreign Ministry says a preliminary assessment conducted under the Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment shows about 7,570 houses were damaged, affecting 32,933 people. Another 48 government officers were affected, as well as 34 miles of roads, 37 drivable bridges and 68 suspension bridges.

Around 4,462 acres of agricultural land, 13 hydropower projects, one solar power plant and two transmission lines were damaged as well, the Foreign Ministry said in a Saturday update.

“Given the scale and extent of the damage caused by this disaster, a comprehensive Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) is being simultaneously undertaken to determine the full extent of loss and damage and the costs for rebuilding and reconstruction,” Nepal’s Foreign Ministry said.

10 दिन पहिने देश मे आयल विनाशकारी बाढ़िक परिणाम स निपटैत रहला पर शनिदिन अलग-अलग अभियान मे दू गोटे कए बचाउल गेल।

द गार्जियन के खबर के अनुसार नेपाली सेना शनिदिन कहलकै कि ओकरऽ सेना आरू दक्षिण कोरियाई आपदा विशेषज्ञऽ स॑ बनलऽ एगो टीम न॑ अपर त्रिशुली-१ जलविद्युत परियोजना म॑ ७४० फुट के सुरंग स॑ एगो चीनी आदमी क॑ बचाबै के काम करलकै । सीएनएन लिखने अछि जे बेतरावटी के चारि मंजिला भवन मे नदी के नीचा एकटा 60 वर्षीय नेपाली महिला भेटल अछि।

सीएनएन के अनुसार, एक स्थानीय अधिकारी कहलनि जे, महिला के परिवार चंडिका श्रेष्ठ हुनकर अंतिम संस्कार के लेल विधिवत अंतिम संस्कार आ तैयारी शुरू केलक, कियाक त हुनका सब के लागल जे हुनकर मौत भ गेल अछि।

जे कहानी महत्व रखै छै ओकरा हेरफेर, पूर्वाग्रह या एजेंडा स॑ मुक्त करै लेली आज ही सीधा तीर ऐप डाउनलोड करी क॑ देखै ल॑ मिलतै ।TM फोन कैमरा क॑ यहाँ इशारा करी क॑ देखै ल॑ मिलतै

अधिकारि सब के कहनाय छनि जे बाढ़ि के कारण कम सं कम 1362 लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि. त्रिशूली नदी क समीप सुविधा पर करीब 900 जलविद्युत मजदूर हजारों लापता मे शामिल छथि।

शुक्रदिन बचावकर्मी त्रिशुली 3ए जलविद्युत संयंत्र मे सुरंग स दूटा मजदूर, एकटा यांत्रिक फोरमैन आ एकटा सुपरवाइजर कए जीवित खींच लेलक। दुनु के हालत स्थिर बताओल जा रहल अछि, आ इलाज के लेल काठमांडू के अस्पताल पहुंचाओल गेल अछि.

नेपाल विद्युत प्राधिकरणके प्रमुख दिर्घायु कुमार श्रेष्ठ जलविद्युत संयंत्रमे सेहो तेसर आदमीके शव बरामद भेल जानकारी द न्यूयॉर्क टाइम्स लिखने अछि । ओ कहलनि जे, ओ आदमी मैकेनिकल इंजीनियर छल।

बचावकर्मी के कहनाय छनि जे शुक्रदिन भोर मे सुरंग के अंदर सं आवाज सुनल गेल, जाहि सं मजदूर के पता लगाबय मे मदद मिलल. बचावकर्मी कहलनि जे, भीतर एखनो आओर आवाज सुनबा मे आबि रहल अछि।

26 अगस्त कए नेपाल-चीन सीमाक समीप हिमनदी ध्वस्त भेलाक बाद आकस्मिक बाढ़ि आ कीचड़क स्खलन शुरू भेल छल ।

नेपाल के विदेश मंत्रालय के कहनाय छनि जे रैपिड डेमेज एंड नीड्स असेसमेंट के तहत कएल गेल प्रारंभिक आकलन मे करीब 7570 घर क्षतिग्रस्त भेल अछि जाहि सं 32,933 लोक प्रभावित भेल अछि. 48टा आओर सरकारी अधिकारी प्रभावित भेलाह, संगहि 34 मील सड़क, 37 ड्राइव करय योग्य पुल आ 68 झूला पुल सेहो प्रभावित भेलाह।

विदेश मंत्रालय शनिदिन जारी अपडेट मे कहलक अछि जे करीब 4,462 एकड़ कृषि भूमि, 13 जलविद्युत परियोजना, एकटा सौर ऊर्जा संयंत्र आ दूटा संचरण लाइन सेहो क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल अछि।

नेपाल केरऽ विदेश मंत्रालय न॑ कहलकै कि ई आपदा स॑ होय वाला नुकसान केरऽ पैमाना आरू विस्तार क॑ देखत॑ हुअ॑ एक साथ व्यापक आपदा बाद जरूरत आकलन (पीडीएनए) करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ताकि नुकसान आरू क्षति केरऽ पूरा विस्तार आरू पुनर्निर्माण आरू पुनर्निर्माण केरऽ खर्च के निर्धारण करलऽ जाय सक॑ ।

title: A local woman is finding ways to help family and community back in Nepal - CBS News
description: A local woman is finding ways to help family and community back in Nepal  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
For Jeena Gurung Vomhof, the Minnesota State Fair was supposed to be a celebration.

A chance to share the art and traditions of the country she still calls home.

Then came devastating news from Nepal.

"I was almost done with the set up to be selling at the 2026 Minnesota State Fair. Excited, pumped, you know, new space, new energy, and I couldn't, I couldn't see my social media, like what's happening. It was like, that was not real to me. And I just called my mom and said what's happening," said Gurung Vomhof.

Gurung Vomhof is originally from Kathmandu.

Nepal is home to Gurung Vomhof's family, her memories, and the women whose work she brings to Minnesota.

"Nepal is a beautiful country. It's an Asian country, right below China and above India, surrounded by beautiful mountains, beautiful people, the tradition, the culture, the love, the humanity that is there in the country I still miss and I try to bring that wherever I go," explained Gurung Vomhof.

Through her business, Namaste Brows & Boutique in Roseville, Gurung Vomhof employs sixteen women in Nepalmaking — hand-crafted earrings, cashmere shawls, hemp, and felt gift items. 100% of the proceeds go back to the makers.

"Each and every piece that I sell has a story," said Gurung Vomhof.

But right now, she's carrying a story of loss.

"My friends, my family, who are far and close, are still back home and we have lost two cousins, 21 and 35, who were going trekking. They're missing," said Gurung Vomhof

She talks with family every day, trying to stay connected while holding herself together.

At the fair, people she doesn't know are giving her something she needs right now.

"My favorite thing right now is hugs. You know, when I'm holding all of this, I don't know how, I have the right word physically, emotionally.

Joy, hurt? That hug means so much," said Gurung Vomhof

Those moments are helping her keep going.

She's already thinking beyond the immediate crisis - about children, education, and rebuilding.

"Education is the root of everything, everything. For me, maybe I can build a classroom, but I can't do it alone. I need all of you," said Gurung Vomhof.

For now, she'll keep standing for Nepal, sharing its culture, and believing in the people standing with her.

"I am at the grandstand at the lower level, row number nine, wide open with colors, with joy, and I'm going to be standing here every single minute," said Gurung Vomhof.

title: UN's Nepal chief makes emotional plea for flood-ravaged country - Yahoo
description: UN's Nepal chief makes emotional plea for flood-ravaged country  Yahoo
publisher.title: Yahoo
full_article:
The United Nations chief in Nepal issued an emotional plea for aid on Sunday, saying survivors of the catastrophic flooding had seen their lives transformed in just "one to two minutes".

After visiting battered mountain communities, UN Resident Coordinator Lila Pieters Yahia told AFP that people were struggling to comprehend how suddenly their Himalayan homes had become an expanse of ruin and destruction.

"You lose your home, you lose your livelihood, you lose your loved one and you lose the breadwinner of your family," Pieters Yahia said in Kathmandu.

"And you know, this happened in one to two minutes."

The devastating August 26 flood that crashed through the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,384 people and left more than 5,500 missing across both countries.

More than 800 foreigners from at least 34 countries are among those missing in both Nepal and Tibet in China. They include both tourists and pilgrims.

Many communities near the epicentre of the disaster remain cut off, with the UN working alongside Nepal's government to get emergency supplies into devastated areas.

The UN has launched a $50 million appeal to help more than 84,000 people affected by the disaster.

"Those people are cut off from the rest of the world because the road is gone," Pieters Yahia said.

"You try to find a solution to expedite access, and you find another bottleneck. We're looking into all means, but we need to to improve access."

- 'Risk of cholera' -

Floods tore through mountain districts, destroying roads, bridges and hydropower dams.

The destruction means journeys that once took a couple of hours have now become day-long ordeals.

"The Himalayas are beautiful, they are amazing, they're spiritual," said Pieters Yahia.

"But also they are very, very difficult terrains... And we have the landslides -- and, plus we're still in the monsoon season."

She warned that beyond immediate shelter and food needs, authorities would have to guard against disease outbreaks and work to protect vulnerable women and girls.

Citing government data, she said 5,000 cattle had died in the flooding.

"This is a big issue because this could lead to communicable diseases... We may have risk of cholera, so this is why immediately we have to invest in sanitation and hygiene."

Pieters Yahia called for greater international support for Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people with limited resources.

"My plea to the international community is: this is the time to help Nepal. It's not tomorrow and it's not yesterday," she said.

"We can't leave them there. We can't leave them alone."

title: China, Nepal race to find thousands still missing 12 days after floods - Al Jazeera
description: China, Nepal race to find thousands still missing 12 days after floods  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
Rescuers in Nepal are racing to reach thousands of people missing in areas near the China border after catastrophic floods as search operations enter their 12th day.

The flooding that authorities say was likely caused by a glacial collapse last month has killed at least 1,384 people and left more than 5,500 missing, among them about 800 foreigners, across the two countries.

Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Families perform symbolic funerals for missing Nepal flood victims

Families perform symbolic funerals for missing Nepal flood victims list 2 of 3 Stranded survivors in Nepal cross raging Trishuli River using zip line

Stranded survivors in Nepal cross raging Trishuli River using zip line list 3 of 3 Is Nepal leading the battle for climate justice? end of list

In Nepal, rescuers have retrieved 1,341 bodies and are searching for about 4,996 people, the national disaster agency said on Sunday. In Tibet, the death toll has risen to 43, with 519 people missing, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.

Four people have been found alive since Friday, three of them in tunnels at hydropower facilities, where the government initially said about 100 people could be alive. Nepal’s Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said teams at flooded hydropower tunnels were facing multiple challenges.

“Search and rescue is going on at the tunnels despite geography, adverse weather and lack of connectivity,” he told the AFP news agency.

On the Chinese side, rescuers face deep mud, poor weather and the risk of further landslides that have slowed work in the narrow gorge.

Nothing remains of a five-storey customs building at Gyirong, once China’s main land port with Nepal, where workers are digging with shovels, excavators and ground-penetrating radar to recover lost people.

The only road into Gyirong reopened on Wednesday, allowing heavy equipment in.

A case of climate justice

Nepal has issued a request that an untested climate emergency mechanism provide aid.

Advertisement

It is asking the United Nations-backed Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage – founded in 2022 to assist developing countries “particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change” – to cover some of the staggering costs of the flood.

The United Nations has appealed for $50m to help more than 84,000 people, saying the destruction makes delivering aid an immense challenge.

On Wednesday, Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal pointed to the role of leading greenhouse gas emitters that have a “historical responsibility to compensate vulnerable nations like Nepal”.

He added that the government has officially filed a “formal climate compensation claim letter” to international partners.

While the exact cause of the glacial collapse remains under investigation, experts say that the frequency and scale of glacier floods have increased as global temperatures have risen.

A United Nations study found that such floods have become nearly five times more frequent since 1950.

Manjeet Dhakal, lead adviser to the UN Least Developed Countries Group on Climate Change, says the global community has a responsibility to cover the cost of disasters afflicting developing nations like Nepal, and that the fund should accept the request.

Countries hit by such disasters are being forced to divert money set aside for health, education and development, he told Al Jazeera. “There are many cases where vulnerable countries are bearing their own cost,” Dhakal said.

The flood was “not caused because of what Nepal has done in the past or in current form”, Dhakal said, noting, “That’s where the global community has a bigger responsibility to come in.”

The UN fund has limited resources, he said. Indeed, its website reflects that it has received only about $631m of $822m in funds pledged by contributing states since inception, and has yet to spend out of the amount.

But, Dhakal said, even a “symbolic amount” could serve as an “inspiring lesson for the fund to justify what it was established for”.

A flood of emotion

Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque, reporting from a Buddhist monastery turned shelter in Kathmandu, said refugees there are still only just beginning to reckon with the trauma of the catastrophe.

“There are people meditating, praying, and there are children. It looks like there is a semblance of normal life,” Haque said. “But make no mistake, I was talking to some of the children here. They’ve lost everything. They’ve lost their families, their homes, their parents.”

About 200 people were brought by helicopter to the holy site, known as the Yellow Monastery, where doctors and volunteers have attended to them.

Advertisement

Haque spoke to a volunteer who had put out drawings for children to express their feelings.

“All of them put their stickers on ‘happy’, he said. Now why is that? The reason, he said, is that the children’s emotions remain suppressed so soon after the crisis,” Haque noted.

“What this volunteer told me is that in the days, months, or years to come, the floods will open, just like the floods open in the Himalayas, and emotions will be poured out.”

नेपाल के बचावकर्मी विनाशकारी बाढ़ के बाद चीन सीमा के पास के इलाका में लापता हजारों लोग के पास पहुंचै के दौड़ में जुटल छै, कैन्हेंकि खोज अभियान १२म दिन में प्रवेश करी रहलऽ छै ।

अधिकारियऽ के कहना छै कि पिछला महीना हिमनदीय गिरला के वजह स॑ जे बाढ़ आबी गेलऽ छै, ओकरा म॑ पूरा दू देश म॑ कम स॑ कम १,३८४ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै आरू ५,५०० स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ लगभग ८०० विदेशी भी शामिल छै ।

अनुशंसित कथा सूची 3 मद सूची 1 मे सँ 3 परिवार लापता नेपाल बाढ़ि पीड़ित के प्रतीकात्मक अंतिम संस्कार करैत अछि |

परिवार सब लापता नेपाल बाढ़ि पीड़ित के प्रतीकात्मक अंतिम संस्कार करैत अछि list 2 of 3 नेपाल में फंसल बचि गेल लोक के जिप लाइन के उपयोग क त्रिशूली नदी पार करैत

नेपाल मे फंसल बचि गेल लोक जिप लाइन के उपयोग क उग्र त्रिशूली नदी पार करैत अछि list 3 of 3 की नेपाल जलवायु न्याय के लड़ाई मे अग्रणी अछि? सूची के अंत

नेपालमे बचावकर्मी १,३४१ शव बरामद कए लगभग ४,९९६ गोटेके खोजमे लागल राष्ट्रिय आपदा एजेन्सी रविदिन जनौलक अछि । चीन के सरकारी समाचार एजेंसी सिन्हुआ के रिपोर्ट के अनुसार तिब्बत में मृतक के संख्या 43 भ गेल अछि, जाहि में 519 लोक लापता अछि।

शुक्रदिन स चारि गोटे जीवित भेटल अछि, जाहि मे तीन गोटे जलविद्युत सुविधा क सुरंग मे अछि, जतय सरकार शुरू मे कहलक जे करीब 100 लोक जीवित भ सकैत अछि। नेपालक ऊर्जा मंत्री विराज भक्त श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, बाढ़ि मे डूबल जलविद्युत सुरंग पर टीम के अनेक चुनौती के सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि।

हुनी एएफपी समाचार एजेंसी स॑ कहलकै कि भूगोल, प्रतिकूल मौसम आरू कनेक्टिविटी के कमी के बावजूद सुरंगऽ प॑ खोज आरू बचाव जारी छै ।

चीनी तरफ स॑ बचावकर्ता सिनी क॑ गहरा कीचड़, खराब मौसम आरू आरू भूस्खलन के खतरा के सामना करना पड़ै छै जेकरा स॑ संकीर्ण गॉर्ज म॑ काम धीमा होय गेलऽ छै ।

नेपाल के साथ कहियो चीन के मुख्य स्थल बंदरगाह ग्यरोंग में पांच मंजिला सीमा शुल्क भवन के किछ नै बचल अछि, जतय मजदूर फावड़ा, खुदाई आ जमीन में घुसय वाला रडार सं खोद क हेरायल लोक के बरामद क रहल छथिन्ह.

बुधदिन ग्यरोंग मे प्रवेश करय वाला एकमात्र सड़क फेर सं खुलल, जाहि सं भारी उपकरण के अंदर घुसय के मौका मिलल.

जलवायु न्याय के एक मामला

नेपाल एकटा अपरीक्षित जलवायु आपातकालीन तंत्र स सहायता प्रदान करबाक आग्रह जारी केलक अछि ।

विज्ञापन

ई संयुक्त राष्ट्र समर्थित फंड फॉर रिस्पांडिंग टू लॉस एंड डेमेज स॑ कहै छै – जेकरऽ स्थापना २०२२ म॑ “जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ प्रतिकूल प्रभाव स॑ विशेष रूप स॑ कमजोर” विकासशील देशऽ क॑ मदद करै लेली करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै – ताकि बाढ़ केरऽ कुछ डगमगाबै वाला लागत क॑ पूरा करलऽ जाय ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र न॑ ८४ हजार स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के मदद लेली ५० मिलियन डॉलर के अपील करलकै आरू कहलकै कि ई तबाही स॑ सहायता पहुँचैना एगो अपार चुनौती बनी गेलऽ छै ।

बुधदिन नेपाल के विदेश मंत्री शिसिर खनाल ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जक के अग्रणी के भूमिका दिस इशारा केलखिन्ह जेकरा पर “नेपाल सन कमजोर राष्ट्र के मुआवजा देबय के ऐतिहासिक जिम्मेदारी” अछि.

हुनी आरू कहलकै कि सरकार नँ आधिकारिक तौर प अंतरराष्ट्रीय भागीदारौ क “औपचारिक जलवायु मुआवजा दावा पत्र” दाखिल करलकै ।

हिमनदी केरऽ पतन केरऽ सही कारण केरऽ जांच जारी छै, लेकिन विशेषज्ञऽ के कहना छै कि वैश्विक तापमान बढ़ला के साथ ही ग्लेशियर केरऽ बाढ़ केरऽ आवृत्ति आरू पैमाना बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ एगो अध्ययन म॑ पता चललै कि 1950 स॑ ही ऐसनऽ बाढ़ लगभग पांच गुना अधिक होय गेलऽ छै ।

जलवायु परिवर्तन पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ अल्पविकसित देश समूह केरऽ प्रमुख सलाहकार मंजीत ढकाल के कहना छै कि नेपाल जैसनऽ विकासशील देशऽ क॑ परेशान करै वाला आपदा केरऽ खर्च पूरा करै के जिम्मेदारी वैश्विक समुदाय के छै, आरू कोष क॑ ई आग्रह क॑ स्वीकार करना चाहियऽ ।

अल जजीरा स॑ बातचीत म॑ हुनी कहलकै कि ऐसनऽ आपदा स॑ प्रभावित देशऽ क॑ स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा आरू विकास लेली अलग करलऽ गेलऽ पैसा क॑ मोड़ै लेली मजबूर करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । ढकल कहलनि जे, बहुत एहन मामला अछि जतय कमजोर देश अपन खर्चा उठा रहल अछि।

बाढ़ि “नेपाल पहिने जे काज केलक अछि या वर्तमान रूप मे केलक ओकर कारण नहि भेल”, ढकाल कहलनि, “ओतहि वैश्विक समुदाय के आबय के पैघ जिम्मेदारी अछि.”

ओ कहला जे संयुक्त राष्ट्र क कोष मे सीमित संसाधन अछि। दरअसल, एकरऽ वेबसाइट स॑ पता चलै छै कि ओकरा शुरू स॑ ही योगदान दै वाला राज्यऽ द्वारा प्रतिज्ञा करलऽ गेलऽ ८२२ मिलियन डॉलर केरऽ फंड म॑ स॑ मात्र लगभग ६३१ मिलियन डॉलर मिललऽ छै, आरू अभी तलक ओकरा ई राशि स॑ बाहर खर्च नै करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

लेकिन, ढकल न॑ कहलकै कि एगो “सांकेतिक राशि” भी “कोष लेली एगो प्रेरणादायक पाठ के रूप म॑ काम करी सकै छै कि ई कोष क॑ जायज ठहराबै के काम करलऽ जाय कि ओकरऽ स्थापना की लेली करलऽ गेलऽ छै” ।

भावुक बाढ़ि

काठमांडू केरऽ बौद्ध मठ स॑ आश्रय देलऽ गेलऽ अल जजीरा केरऽ निकोलस हक न॑ कहलकै कि वहाँ के शरणार्थी अभी भी प्रलय केरऽ आघात के हिसाब लगाना शुरू करी रहलऽ छै ।

हक कहलनि जे, लोक ध्यान करैत छथि, प्रार्थना करैत छथि, आ बच्चा सेहो अछि, लगैत अछि जेना सामान्य जीवनक आभास अछि। “मुदा गलती नहि करू, हम एत’क किछु बच्चा सभ सँ गप्प क’ रहल छलहुँ, सब किछु गमा लेलक, परिवार, घर, माता-पिता केँ गमा लेलक।”

लगभग 200 लोगऽ क॑ हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ ई पवित्र स्थल प॑ लानलऽ गेलै, जेकरा पीला मठ के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै, जहां डॉक्टर आरू स्वयंसेवक न॑ हुनकऽ देखभाल करी चुकलऽ छै ।

विज्ञापन

हक एकटा स्वयंसेवक स गप केलथि जे बच्चा सब लेल ड्राइंग लगा क अपन भावना व्यक्त केने छलाह।

ओ कहलनि जे, सब अपन स्टिकर ‘हैप्पी’ पर लगा देलनि। आब से किएक? हुनकऽ कहना छै कि एकरऽ कारण ई छै कि संकट के बाद भी बच्चा सिनी के भावना एतना जल्दी दबाय देलऽ जाय छै,’’ हक न॑ नोट करलकै ।

“ई स्वयंसेवक हमरा जे कहलक से ई जे आबै बला दिन, महीना, वा साल मे बाढ़ि खुजत, ठीक ओहिना जेना हिमालय मे बाढ़ि खुजत, आ भाव उझलि जायत।”

title: Nepal-China border floods death toll climbs to 1,385 as thousands remain missing - TRT World
description: Nepal-China border floods death toll climbs to 1,385 as thousands remain missing  TRT World
publisher.title: TRT World
full_article:
The death toll from devastating flash floods in Nepal has reached at least 1,342, with thousands still missing, officials and local media reports have said.

The combined death toll from flash floods and mudslides along the Nepal-China border rose to at least 1,385, while 5,519 people remained missing 11 days after the disaster struck, according to official data from the two countries on Sunday.

Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said around 5,000 people, including 589 foreigners, remained missing.

More than 13,000 people have so far been rescued from the flood-hit areas.

Chinese authorities said at least 43 people have been confirmed dead, while 519 others remained missing in Tibet.

Of those missing, 850 are foreigners, according to official figures from Nepal and China.

Related TRT World - Rescuers pull Chinese national alive from Nepal tunnel after 10 days

‘We are not getting enough to eat’

With roads and bridges damaged due to massive floods and landslides, thousands of expectant and new mothers are struggling hardest to find a female-friendly space to breastfeed, get proper food and reach emergency care if labour turns dangerous, the local English daily Kathmandu Post reported.

The mothers also complain about cigarette smoke, the smell of alcohol and, on top of all that, unhygienic food and water, which upset their and their babies' stomachs.

Also, there are no vaccination facilities for children in the shelter camps.

"We are not getting food on time either. We are not getting enough to eat,” a new mother who wished to be identified only as Pariyar said.

Pariyar fled her home when floods struck her hometown, Trishuli, on the morning of August 26 and is now staying with dozens of strangers under one roof in a shelter camp.

title: Chinese worker rescued after 10 days trapped in Nepal tunnel - kmph.com
description: Chinese worker rescued after 10 days trapped in Nepal tunnel  kmph.com
publisher.title: kmph.com
full_article:
(TNND) — Ten days after catastrophic flash floods tore through Nepal’s mountains, rescuers pulled a Chinese worker from a mud-filled hydropower tunnel, a rare moment of relief amid a disaster that has killed more than 1,300 people and left thousands unaccounted for.

The flash floods struck Nepal and China’s Tibet region on Aug. 26, likely after a glacier collapse. Nepal’s disaster management agency said nearly 4,900 people remain missing. Earlier in the response, authorities reported more than 3,700 people had been rescued in Nepal.

On the Tibet side of the border, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported 43 deaths and 519 people missing as of Saturday evening. CCTV said 261 of those missing were foreigners.

Rescue operations have focused in part on hydropower sites in Nepal’s Rasuwa district and the devastated Gyirong border crossing in Tibet. Authorities previously believed more than 100 people could be trapped inside a mud-filled tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project.

CCTV reported that Lu Haitao, a 49-year-old Chinese worker, was rescued Saturday from a 225-meter, or roughly 740-foot, hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa, 10 days after the floods. Rescuers carried Lu out of the tunnel and evacuated him by helicopter, according to CCTV, which reported he was hospitalized in stable condition.

Lu told CCTV he had climbed to the highest point in the tunnel and had begun to lose hope before rescue crews found him. CCTV reported Lu is a former farmer from Henan province who also worked as a carpenter, and that he traveled to Nepal in February for his first job abroad.

As the search continues, families of missing people have searched hospitals and relief centers and posted photographs and contact information in hopes of finding relatives.

Rescue work has been complicated by steep mountains, narrow gorges and concern about further flooding from a lake that formed in the Himalayas after the initial disaster. Chinese monitoring data showed the water level in that new lake had dropped about 10 meters, or 32 feet, from its peak.

Nepal said it mobilized domestic and international resources, including an 11-member tunnel-rescue reconnaissance team from India. A similar team from China was expected.

Nepal has received more than 57 metric tons of relief supplies from India, with aid also arriving from China, Japan, Australia and other countries.

लू सीसीटीवी क॑ बतैलकै कि हुनी सुरंग केरऽ सबस॑ ऊँचऽ बिंदु प॑ चढ़ी गेलऽ छै आरू बचाव दल न॑ ओकरा मिलै स॑ पहल॑ ही उम्मीद खोना शुरू करी देल॑ छै । सीसीटीवी केरऽ रिपोर्ट छै कि लु हेनान प्रांत केरऽ पूर्व किसान छै जे बढ़ई के काम भी करै छेलै, आरू वू फरवरी म॑ विदेश म॑ अपनऽ पहिलऽ नौकरी लेली नेपाल गेलऽ छेलै ।

तलाशी जारी रहला पर लापता लोक के परिवार अस्पताल आ राहत केंद्र के तलाशी लेलक आ रिश्तेदार के खोजय के उम्मीद मे फोटो आओर संपर्क जानकारी पोस्ट केलक अछि.

खड़ा पहाड़, संकीर्ण गॉर्ज आरू प्रारंभिक आपदा के बाद हिमालय म॑ बनलऽ झील स॑ आरू बाढ़ के चिंता के कारण बचाव के काम जटिल होय गेलऽ छै । चीनी निगरानी केरऽ आंकड़ा स॑ पता चललै कि पानी केरऽ स्तर ई बात स॑ पता चललै कि नया झील अपनऽ चरम स॑ लगभग १० मीटर यानी ३२ फीट गिरी गेलऽ छै ।

title: Photos: UN urges global aid after China, Nepal floods kill over 1,300 - Al Jazeera
description: Photos: UN urges global aid after China, Nepal floods kill over 1,300  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
The United Nations’ top official in Nepal has issued an emotional appeal for international aid, warning that survivors of the catastrophic Himalayan flooding last month saw their lives transformed “in one to two minutes”.

The UN Resident Coordinator, Lila Pieters Yahia, said communities along the China-Nepal border were struggling to comprehend the scale of devastation after torrential floods on August 26 tore through mountain districts, destroying roads, bridges and hydropower dams.

“You lose your home, you lose your livelihood, you lose your loved one and you lose the breadwinner of your family,” she told the AFP news agency in Kathmandu. “And you know, this happened in one to two minutes.”

At least 1,384 people were killed and more than 5,500 others remain missing in Nepal and the Tibet region of China. Among the missing are more than 800 foreigners from at least 34 countries, including tourists and pilgrims.

Many communities near the epicentre remain cut off, with roads washed away and journeys that once took hours now stretching into days. The UN, working with Nepal’s government, has launched a $50m appeal to support more than 84,000 people affected.

The UN’s Pieters Yahia warned of the risk of cholera and other communicable diseases, citing the deaths of 5,000 cattle and urging urgent investment in sanitation, hygiene and protection for vulnerable women and girls.

“My plea to the international community is: this is the time to help Nepal,” she said. “We can’t leave them alone.”

title: Death toll from Nepal floods rises to 1,341 as rescue operations continue - sana.sy
description: Death toll from Nepal floods rises to 1,341 as rescue operations continue  sana.sy
publisher.title: sana.sy
full_article:
Kathmandu, Sept. 6 (SANA) The death toll from devastating floods that struck mountain valleys in Nepal along the border with China has risen to at least 1,341, with nearly 5,000 people reported missing as search and rescue operations continue.

Citing a provisional tally released Sunday by Nepal‘s emergency response authority, Agence France-Presse reported that a wall of water, ice, and debris swept through northern valleys, leaving 1,341 dead and 4,996 missing. Those missing include hundreds of foreign tourists as well as approximately 900 workers stationed at power plants and dam sites at the time of the disaster.

Nepali Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha confirmed that rescue teams are working around the clock 11 days after the disaster struck. He noted that operations are currently focused on power project tunnels despite severe geographical obstacles, bad weather, and a total collapse of local communications.

Shrestha added that large helicopters can no longer land at two key sites to deliver heavy equipment, though teams are evaluating alternative methods to advance the operation. Rescue workers recently pulled three survivors from the Trishuli-3 dam project tunnels—two Nepali workers and a Chinese national—and rescued a woman in her 60s from a mud-buried home.

Preliminary official estimates place the economic damage to housing, infrastructure, and property at a minimum of 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees (approximately $2.56 billion). The disaster was triggered on Aug. 26 when flash floods, mudslides, and rockfalls swept through Himalayan border districts, severing roads, power supply, and communications.

title: Photos: UN urges global aid after China, Nepal floods kill over 1,300 - aljazeera.com
description: Photos: UN urges global aid after China, Nepal floods kill over 1,300  aljazeera.com
publisher.title: aljazeera.com
full_article:
The United Nations’ top official in Nepal has issued an emotional appeal for international aid, warning that survivors of the catastrophic Himalayan flooding last month saw their lives transformed “in one to two minutes”.

The UN Resident Coordinator, Lila Pieters Yahia, said communities along the China-Nepal border were struggling to comprehend the scale of devastation after torrential floods on August 26 tore through mountain districts, destroying roads, bridges and hydropower dams.

“You lose your home, you lose your livelihood, you lose your loved one and you lose the breadwinner of your family,” she told the AFP news agency in Kathmandu. “And you know, this happened in one to two minutes.”

At least 1,384 people were killed and more than 5,500 others remain missing in Nepal and the Tibet region of China. Among the missing are more than 800 foreigners from at least 34 countries, including tourists and pilgrims.

Many communities near the epicentre remain cut off, with roads washed away and journeys that once took hours now stretching into days. The UN, working with Nepal’s government, has launched a $50m appeal to support more than 84,000 people affected.

The UN’s Pieters Yahia warned of the risk of cholera and other communicable diseases, citing the deaths of 5,000 cattle and urging urgent investment in sanitation, hygiene and protection for vulnerable women and girls.

“My plea to the international community is: this is the time to help Nepal,” she said. “We can’t leave them alone.”

title: Middle Tennessee woman among spiritual travelers who died in Nepal flood - Chattanooga Times Free Press
description: Middle Tennessee woman among spiritual travelers who died in Nepal flood  Chattanooga Times Free Press
publisher.title: Chattanooga Times Free Press
full_article:
As soon as Leslie Crespi heard the news about the floods in Nepal, she put on her shoes and ran out her door to make her way to a friend’s house. On Aug. 26, flash flooding on the Nepal-China border led to buildings and towns being washed away, and the combined death toll has surpassed 950 people as of Monday, according to the Associated Press. At the time the flood hit, a group of 80 people from the Isha Foundation — 77 travelers and three volunteers who were helping guide the group — were at a Chinese immigration center at the Nepal-China border, returning from their two-week trip. Officials told the Isha Foundation that there is no indication of survivors in the area, Crespi said. Out of the 77 travelers, 22 were American, 12 were Canadian and the rest of the group was made up of people from 19 other countries, Crespi said. Crespi serves as the community liaison for the Isha Institute of Inner-Sciences, a center dedicated to classical yoga and meditation practices with the goal of raising human consciousness, she said. The center, based in McMinnville, Tennessee, is part of the international Isha Foundation, which had groups of people traveling in the Himalayas on what the organization calls a sojourn to Lake Manasarovar and Mount Kailash in Tibet. The foundation is not releasing the identities of those who were lost in the floods out of respect for their families. Many of the Americans and Canadians who were at the flooded immigration center had come through the center in McMinnville, Crespi said, so the news brings personal grief. “Initially, when we first heard the information, everybody goes into shock,” Crespi said. “This was so unexpected and the hit on that building was so devastating that it’s hard to take in, but we had to support the families immediately.” One of the 22 Americans on the sojourn was a wife and mother from Middle Tennessee, Crespi said, and the woman’s husband and family were Crespi’s first visit. Crespi, alongside other volunteers, has been gathering information from authorities in China and Nepal and distributing it to families in the days following the catastrophe. “Just a lot of silent support,” Crespi said. “Honestly, we were trying to do whatever was needed in each situation.” The Isha Foundation was established 30 years ago, Crespi said, by Sadhguru (born Jagadish Vasudev), an Indian spiritual guru. There are five main centers, two in the United States — in Los Angeles, California, and McMinnville, Tennessee. The Institute of Inner-Sciences in McMinnville was established in 2005, Crespi said. The foundation has been doing this type of trip for 21 years, she said. The people on the trip came from all walks of life — all kinds of religions, traditions, nationalities and ages. Crespi herself has been to Kailash twice. “Being on that soil, walking on that soil, looking at the faces of those people, those gentle, beautiful people that are there … these are the people that are from the region that support you along the journey,” Crespi said. “It’s heartbreaking because, you know, this is a hugely spiritual part of the world, and to see to see the level of devastation right now, it’s humongous.” There were more than 700 additional travelers with the Isha Foundation and Sadhguru still on the Tibet side when the floods hit, Crespi said. Those people were all safe, and are on their way back to their homes. Since the flooding, Sadhguru hosted an event in Kathmandu called “In Solidarity with Nepal,” calling for nations around the world to support the region, Crespi said. The plan was for this year to be Sadhguru’s last sojourn, but now, he plans to return, Crespi said. “Looking at the scale of destruction, it looks bad,” Sadhguru said in a video message recorded on Aug. 26 and posted to the Isha Foundation’s website. “The same building where we were for immigration just a week ago, that entire building is washed away, and part of the town is washed away.” The guru had tears in his eyes as he choked through the information he had on the group, and the audience behind the camera can be heard weeping. Sadhguru said in the video that he had passed by the group while they were on their way down Mount Kailash and he and his group were on their way up. Sadhguru recieved a message from the group’s guide at 9:05 a.m. that they had arrived at the immigration center, and the floods swept through at 9:14 a.m., he said in the video. The guide had a Nepali phone that would have become active if the group had crossed over into the country, but the phone never came online, Sadhguru said. The first day or two were dedicated to relaying information to families, but now, the reality is sinking in. Crespi is leaning on the yoga and meditation techniques she learned when she first came to the Isha Foundation over 20 years ago, she said, to handle the grief. “Right now for me, I’m recognizing the painful reality of the situation,” Crespi said. “At 42, I learned to meditate, and I have to tell you, it’s been an anchoring thing for me throughout this. It keeps me at a certain level of centeredness and clarity and perception. It doesn’t mean there’s no pain. There’s definitely a deep pain and compassion, but there’s a certain stability that moves you forward, and that has been a godsend.” Contact faith and family editor Kailee Shores at kshores@timesfreepress.com or 423-757-6659.

title: Chinese worker rescued after 10 days trapped in Nepal tunnel - KHGI
description: Chinese worker rescued after 10 days trapped in Nepal tunnel  KHGI
publisher.title: KHGI
full_article:
(TNND) — Ten days after catastrophic flash floods tore through Nepal’s mountains, rescuers pulled a Chinese worker from a mud-filled hydropower tunnel, a rare moment of relief amid a disaster that has killed more than 1,300 people and left thousands unaccounted for.

The flash floods struck Nepal and China’s Tibet region on Aug. 26, likely after a glacier collapse. Nepal’s disaster management agency said nearly 4,900 people remain missing. Earlier in the response, authorities reported more than 3,700 people had been rescued in Nepal.

On the Tibet side of the border, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported 43 deaths and 519 people missing as of Saturday evening. CCTV said 261 of those missing were foreigners.

Rescue operations have focused in part on hydropower sites in Nepal’s Rasuwa district and the devastated Gyirong border crossing in Tibet. Authorities previously believed more than 100 people could be trapped inside a mud-filled tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project.

CCTV reported that Lu Haitao, a 49-year-old Chinese worker, was rescued Saturday from a 225-meter, or roughly 740-foot, hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa, 10 days after the floods. Rescuers carried Lu out of the tunnel and evacuated him by helicopter, according to CCTV, which reported he was hospitalized in stable condition.

Lu told CCTV he had climbed to the highest point in the tunnel and had begun to lose hope before rescue crews found him. CCTV reported Lu is a former farmer from Henan province who also worked as a carpenter, and that he traveled to Nepal in February for his first job abroad.

As the search continues, families of missing people have searched hospitals and relief centers and posted photographs and contact information in hopes of finding relatives.

Rescue work has been complicated by steep mountains, narrow gorges and concern about further flooding from a lake that formed in the Himalayas after the initial disaster. Chinese monitoring data showed the water level in that new lake had dropped about 10 meters, or 32 feet, from its peak.

Nepal said it mobilized domestic and international resources, including an 11-member tunnel-rescue reconnaissance team from India. A similar team from China was expected.

Nepal has received more than 57 metric tons of relief supplies from India, with aid also arriving from China, Japan, Australia and other countries.

नेपाल आरू चीन केरऽ तिब्बत क्षेत्र म॑ २६ अगस्त क॑ आकस्मिक बाढ़ आबी गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरऽ संभावना ग्लेशियर केरऽ गिरला के बाद होय गेलऽ छै । नेपाल के आपदा प्रबंधन एजेंसी के कहनाय छनि जे करीब 4900 लोक लापता अछि. एहि सं पहिने प्रतिक्रिया मे अधिकारी नेपाल मे 3700 सं बेसि लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि.

सीमा के तिब्बत तरफ चीनी सरकारी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी में शनिदिन साँझ तक 43 लोक के मौत आ 519 लोक के लापता होय के खबर अछि. सीसीटीवी के कहनाय अछि जे लापता मे सं 261 गोटे विदेशी छथिन्ह.

बचाव कार्य कुछ हद तक नेपाल केरऽ रसुवा जिला केरऽ जलविद्युत स्थल आरू तिब्बत केरऽ तबाह ग्यरोंग सीमा पार प॑ केंद्रित छै । अधिकारि सब के पहिने विश्वास छल जे अपर त्रिशुली-1 जलविद्युत परियोजना के कीचड़ सं भरल सुरंग के अंदर 100 सं बेसी लोक फंसल भ सकैत अछि.

सीसीटीवी के खबर छै कि बाढ़ के 10 दिन बाद शनिदिन रसुवा के 225 मीटर यानी लगभग 740 फीट के जलविद्युत सुरंग स॑ 49 वर्षीय चीनी मजदूर लु हैताओ क॑ बचाय लेलऽ गेलै । सीसीटीवी के अनुसार बचावकर्मी लु क॑ सुरंग स॑ बाहर निकाली क॑ हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ बाहर निकाली लेलकै, जेकरा म॑ हुनकऽ हालत स्थिर अस्पताल म॑ भर्ती होय के खबर छै ।

लू सीसीटीवी क॑ बतैलकै कि हुनी सुरंग केरऽ सबस॑ ऊँचऽ बिंदु प॑ चढ़ी गेलऽ छै आरू बचाव दल न॑ ओकरा मिलै स॑ पहल॑ ही उम्मीद खोना शुरू करी देल॑ छै । सीसीटीवी केरऽ रिपोर्ट छै कि लु हेनान प्रांत केरऽ पूर्व किसान छै जे बढ़ई के काम भी करै छेलै, आरू वू फरवरी म॑ विदेश म॑ अपनऽ पहिलऽ नौकरी लेली नेपाल गेलऽ छेलै ।

तलाशी जारी रहला पर लापता लोक के परिवार अस्पताल आ राहत केंद्र के तलाशी लेलक आ रिश्तेदार के खोजय के उम्मीद मे फोटो आओर संपर्क जानकारी पोस्ट केलक अछि.

खड़ा पहाड़, संकीर्ण गॉर्ज आरू प्रारंभिक आपदा के बाद हिमालय म॑ बनलऽ झील स॑ आरू बाढ़ के चिंता के कारण बचाव के काम जटिल होय गेलऽ छै । चीनी निगरानी केरऽ आंकड़ा स॑ पता चललै कि पानी केरऽ स्तर ई बात स॑ पता चललै कि नया झील अपनऽ चरम स॑ लगभग १० मीटर यानी ३२ फीट गिरी गेलऽ छै ।

नेपाल भारत सँ ११ सदस्यीय सुरंग-बचाव टोही दल सहित घरेलु आ अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय संसाधन जुटाओल गेल बतौलक अछि । चीन स सेहो एहने टीम क उम्मीद छल।

नेपाल भारत सँ ५७ मीट्रिक टन सँ बेसी राहत सामग्री प्राप्त केलक अछि, चीन, जापान, ऑस्ट्रेलिया आ अन्य देश सँ सेहो सहायता पहुँचल अछि ।

title: Nepal Flood Disaster - Caritas Australia
description: Nepal Flood Disaster  Caritas Australia
publisher.title: Caritas Australia
full_article:
The full scale of the disaster is continuing to emerge. Hundreds of people have been killed and thousands are missing. Entire communities have been destroyed, roads and bridges have been washed away, and thousands of families have been displaced.

The disaster was triggered by a massive flood surge through the Bhote Koshi River on 26 August, devastating communities across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and other downstream districts. Rescue operations remain underway, but damaged infrastructure and ongoing flood risks continue to limit access to many affected communities.

The humanitarian needs remain immense. Families urgently require food, clean water, shelter, health care and essential household items. Schools and health facilities have also been damaged, and humanitarian assessments indicate that thousands of children need support.

ई आपदा 26 अगस्त क॑ भोटे कोशी नदी के माध्यम स॑ भारी बाढ़ के लहर स॑ शुरू होय गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ पूरा रसुवा, नुवाकोट, धडिंग आरू अन्य डाउनस्ट्रीम जिला के समुदाय तबाह होय गेलऽ छेलै । बचाव अभियान जारी छै, लेकिन क्षतिग्रस्त बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू जारी बाढ़ के जोखिम के कारण बहुत प्रभावित समुदायऽ तलक पहुँच सीमित होय रहलऽ छै ।

मानवीय आवश्यकता अपार बनल अछि। परिवारक कें तत्काल भोजन, स्वच्छ पानी, आवास, स्वास्थ्य देखभाल आ आवश्यक घरेलू सामान कें आवश्यकता होयत छै. स्कूल आ स्वास्थ्य सुविधाक कें सेहो नुकसान पहुंचल छै, आ मानवीय आकलन सं पता चलय छै कि हजारक बच्चाक कें सहायता कें जरूरत छै.

title: Connecticut’s Nepali community holds vigil for flood victims - wfsb.com
description: Connecticut’s Nepali community holds vigil for flood victims  wfsb.com
publisher.title: wfsb.com
full_article:
WEST HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - Connecticut’s Nepali community gathered Sunday evening at West Hartford Town Hall for a candlelight vigil honoring those killed and missing after flash floods in Nepal’s Bhote Koshi Valley.

Dozens attended the vigil, and organizers said the gathering was meant to remember those who lost their lives and to support families still waiting for answers.

Families await word from Nepal

Many families in Connecticut’s Nepali community have relatives and friends in the areas hit by the floods, and some are still waiting to hear from loved ones.

As of Sept. 3, Nepal’s disaster authority reported about 1,252 people dead and more than 4,200 people still missing.

Vigil draws young and old

Those gathered said they are holding on to hope and doing what they can to support those affected back home.

Bishesh Pariyar, 8, said, “I just feel sad, worried about all my family stuck in Nepal with the flood.”

Kashbi Kandel, 14, said, “We’re sending prayers for them, hoping their okay and everything will be okay and we will move past this.”

title: Bangladesh sought more energy from Nepal, but floods have halted exports - Eco-Business
description: Bangladesh sought more energy from Nepal, but floods have halted exports  Eco-Business
publisher.title: Eco-Business
full_article:
Monsoon rains have routinely given Nepal a surge of hydropower, creating a surplus. Some of that surplus was used to supplement downstream neighbour Bangladesh’s fossil-fuel-dependent electricity supply.

On 26 August, however, Nepal’s hydropower system was damaged extensively. Flash floods swept through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems, killing at least 1,250 people as of 3 September. The floods also damaged 15 hydropower plants and critical transmission infrastructure, wiping out over 750 MW of electricity generation, reported Time. Nearly 900 hydropower workers are missing.

The disaster has now disrupted Nepal’s electricity exports, with supplies to Bangladesh halted, authorities in Dhaka and Kathmandu confirmed to Dialogue Earth.

On 3 September, Shaligram Bhandari, a spokesperson for Nepal’s Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, told Dialogue Earth that floods damaged the 22 megawatt (MW) Chilime and 24 MW Trishuli hydropower projects, which have since stopped generating electricity. The power they produced had been approved for export to Bangladesh. Nepal halted all power exports, Reuters reported several days earlier.

Amid the disaster, the ministry had yet to explore alternatives, Bhandari said.

Nepal’s growing role as a hydropower exporter must be viewed together with these vulnerabilities.

“ Hydropower from Nepal and Bhutan could provide Bangladesh with a cheaper source of electricity than many of the country’s existing generation sources. Shafiqul Alam, lead analyst for Bangladesh, Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis

Complicating its role as an exporter is its lack of a shared border with Bangladesh. Electricity trade between them has passed through India’s transmission network, which comes with some conditions.

Since 2024, Nepal has been exporting 40 MW of electricity to Bangladesh through India’s network every June to November. It wanted to export 20 MW more. But this June, the Indian power trading company which manages cross-border grid operations with Bangladesh declined the request, Nepali government officials told the Kathmandu Post. The company, NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited, reportedly cited capacity constraints on the India-Bangladesh transmission line.

In July, India held energy cooperation talks with Nepal. While there was development on bilateral energy coordination, there was no resolution on the 20 MW issue.

That amount is minuscule compared to the size of the three countries’ electricity grids, which have a combined total installed capacity of around 586 GW. But energy experts, officials and power-sector analysts in those countries told Dialogue Earth the 20 MW impasse is more nuanced than it appears. There are technical, procedural and political factors at play, they note.

The disruption in Nepal comes at a particularly difficult time for Bangladesh, which has experienced severe load-shedding in recent days. It faced a power shortfall exceeding 3,500 MW at one point, as well as widespread outages across the country. The loss of electricity from Nepal only adds to that pressure.

While Bangladeshi and Nepali experts point to unused capacity on the India-Bangladesh transmission link, Indian experts say there could be a genuine capacity limitation on the line. In the absence of a regional body and trade mechanism dedicated to energy, procedural lapses and politics also have major roles to play, they note. Strained India-Bangladesh relations since Bangladesh’s 2024 change of government may also be involved.

Why Bangladesh wants Nepal’s hydropower

Nepal and Bangladesh have complementary electricity needs. The summer monsoon gives Nepal surplus hydropower, which Bangladesh can use to diversify its energy sources. In the dry winter, these roles reverse somewhat – Nepal faces shortages while Bangladesh’s demand dips – making cross-border trade beneficial in both directions over the year.

In 2025-2026, Nepal’s total installed capacity reached 4.1 GW, but monthly peak domestic demand stood at only around 2.5 GW, according to the Nepal Energy Authority. Electricity exports bring total demand up to about 3.2 GW.

Bangladesh has 32 GW of installed power generation capacity, 98 per cent of which is dependent on fossil fuels, according to energy think-tank Ember. The country wants to diversify sources to meet its current demand. Bangladesh also aims to cover 20 per cent of its electricity needs from non-imported renewables by 2030. Energy trade between Nepal and Bangladesh therefore makes “economic sense”, says Shahriar Ahmed Chowdhury, director of the Centre for Energy Research at United International University in Dhaka. “Hydropower from Nepal and Bhutan could provide Bangladesh with a cheaper source of electricity than many of the country’s existing generation sources,” says Shafiqul Alam, lead analyst for Bangladesh energy at the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis. “Ideally, electricity trade should work both ways,” Chowdhury says. But expanding such trade is “a political decision”, he notes. “The volume is small, but it is important because it marks the beginning of cross-border electricity cooperation.” Cross-border electricity trade helps Bangladesh primarily by shielding it from geopolitical disruptions to energy supplies, volatility in international fuel prices and diversification, experts say. After all, the additional 20 MW will not help Bangladesh meet its 20 per cent renewables target. There is no plan to include imports within what is a domestic generation target, says Aninda Islam Amit, Bangladesh’s state minister for power, energy and mineral resources. He expects the country’s private sector to “take the lead” on renewables as there are “incentives for private entrepreneurs”, he tells Dialogue Earth. For Nepal, the energy trade is part of a much larger ambition. During the July energy talks, it agreed to increase its export capacity as India ups its import capacity. Nepali energy minister Birajbhakta Shrestha tells Dialogue Earth that the deal is another step towards fulfilling the country’s agreement to export 10 GW of electricity to India, signed in 2024. A Nepali energy ministry official, requesting anonymity, says the immediate 20-MW issue could be resolved through trilateral discussions between Nepal, India and Bangladesh. India holds the missing link The 40 MW Nepal currently exports to Bangladesh is transported by the Baharampur-Bheramara high-voltage DC interconnection from east India, where it arrives on a transmission line from southern Nepal. The Baharampur-Bheramara link between India and Bangladesh has a transfer capacity of 1 GW. The country typically receives around 920-930 MW through the link, leaving some unused transfer capacity, said a Bangladesh Power Division official speaking on condition of anonymity. Nepal has also been considering alternatives. “If power cannot be exported via the Baharampur-Bheramara line, there is option for Nepal to export the additional 20 MW through other Indian transmission lines connected to Bangladesh,” says Manoj Silwal, former deputy managing director of the Nepal Electricity Authority. Apart from the Baharampur-Bheramara link, Bangladesh also imports nearly 1.7 GW from India: 160 MW through the Surajmaninagar to Comilla interconnection, and 1.5 GW from Godda to Rohanpur, the latter operated by Adani Power. However, transporting the 20 MW via existing corridors may not be feasible for a few reasons, says Nikit Abhyankar, an energy efficiency expert at the University of California, Berkeley. It is possible that these corridors are fully utilised. Additionally, the average amount of electricity a transmission line carries is not necessarily the capacity that is safely available, Abhyankar notes. At times of peak demand, power flows can be much higher, and some capacity must be reserved to manage unexpected failures elsewhere in the system. “I would be very surprised if they are actually going to operate a 1,000 MW line at 1,000 MW capacity,” Abhyankar says. A line may also be unable to deliver its rated amount of electricity due to losses from transfers. In a high-voltage DC connection, such as Baharampur-Bheramara, some electricity is lost when power is converted from AC to DC, as it travels along the transmission line, and when converted back to AC at the receiving end. Abhyankar estimates that roughly 40-50 MW could be lost on a 1-GW line. The Baharampur-Bheramara corridor is also loaded with India’s own exports to Bangladesh. India’s Central Electricity Authority “doesn’t want to run the line close to its thermal limit … on a line that also carries India’s own bilateral exports”, notes Binit Das, deputy programme manager for renewable energy at the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE). For the India-Bangladesh link, battery storage could potentially help if the line has spare capacity during periods of lower demand, Abhyankar adds. But feasibility depends on how much the power flow on the interconnection varies over the day. Politics complicates power trade Geography presents India with an unavoidable role in any future Nepal-Bangladesh electricity trade. “There is no other way that Bangladesh can get power from either Nepal or Bhutan without that being facilitated by India,” says Bipul Chattopadhyay, executive director of the Consumer Unity & Trust Society (CUTS), India. Experts see this 20 MW episode as a litmus test for how India prioritises capacity across competing uses of a shared asset. During this impasse, India and Nepal separately reached a much bigger capacity decision: to raise Nepal’s export quota from 1.1 GW to 1.65 GW. “The asymmetry between how quickly that bilateral decision happened and how long the trilateral 20 MW has languished is itself the clearest evidence of where the region’s integration problem actually sits,” says Das of the CSE. India’s role in Nepal’s hydropower sector also complicates the picture. Several Indian companies are developing major hydropower projects in Nepal, while India is also Nepal’s principal electricity export market and the transit country for its exports to Bangladesh. India could increasingly draw on Nepal’s hydropower to meet its own rising demand, Chattopadhyay says. The challenge is to develop a framework that works for all the countries involved. “It should be win-win for all three parties,” he says. “That model is not difficult to develop, but that is something which is still missing in our current political-economic discourse.” He also raises political considerations in the 20-MW denial. Relations between India and Bangladesh have been strained since former prime minister of Bangladesh, Sheikh Hasina, went into exile in India in August 2024, where she remains. “After the change in government in Bangladesh, [the] India-Bangladesh relationship is yet to get on the right track … it’s very frosty,” notes Chattopadhyay. A South Asian electricity market? The difficulty of moving a mere 20 MW points to bottlenecks in cross-border energy trade in a region with growing energy needs. Every prior expansion of the transmission corridor, including the original 40 MW, was formalised through a Joint Steering Committee (JSC) decision followed by a tripartite agreement. The 13th Nepal-India JSC meeting was held in July, having last convened in February 2025, but failed to yield success with the 20 MW addition. There is also a broader institutional problem. Cross-border electricity trade between Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal, where it goes through India, requires multiple layers of approval. This includes a tripartite power sale agreement, clearance from India’s Central Electricity Authority and a JSC to anchor the decision. Over the last few years, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal have signed bilateral agreements with India to develop electricity trade. As of April, India has entered into 17 power-sector agreements with neighbouring countries. It is also involved in 13 cross-border power-generation projects and 30 transmission-link projects. Trilateral and regional transactions carry a layer of political and procedural friction that bilateral ones don’t, Das says. This makes the region’s power systems interconnected yet fragmented. The potential benefits of deeper integration are significant. Cross-border electricity trade can allow these countries to complement one another’s demands, reducing reliance on fossil fuels while improving energy security and lowering costs, joint research by CUTS and Chintan Research Foundation found. The stakes are also different for countries of different sizes. “For a large system like India … small cross-border trade doesn’t really make a huge difference. But for countries like Nepal to sell their hydroelectricity [and] for countries like Bangladesh to meet their electricity demand reliably, cross-border trade becomes important,” says Abhyankar. Yet there is still no subregional institution focused on coordinating and facilitating cross-border electricity trade. A regional power exchange, an agreed open-access framework, or institutionalised, calendar-bound trilateral bodies could provide a more predictable way of handling third-country transit, says Das. “Without such a mechanism, episodes like the 20-MW holdup could continue to recur even as the region’s growing hydropower surplus and complementary electricity demand make the case for trade increasingly obvious,” he says. परिवहन किछ कारण सं संभव नहिं भ सकैत अछि. संभव अछि जे एहि गलियारा क पूर्ण उपयोग होए। एकरऽ अलावा, एक ट्रांसमिशन लाइन म॑ औसतन बिजली के मात्रा जरूरी नै छै कि वू क्षमता सुरक्षित रूप स॑ उपलब्ध होय, अभ्यंकर न॑ नोट करलकै । पीक डिमांड कें समय बिजली कें प्रवाह बहुत बेसि भ सकय छै, आ सिस्टम मे अन्य जगहक पर अप्रत्याशित विफलता कें प्रबंधन कें लेल किच्छू क्षमता आरक्षित करनाय आवश्यक छै. अभिनकर कहैत छथि जे अगर ओ वास्तव मे 1000 मेगावाट क क्षमता पर 1000 मेगावाट क लाइन चलाबए जा रहल छथि त हमरा बहुत आश्चर्य होएत। कोनों लाइन ट्रांसफर सं नुकसान कें कारण अपन रेटेड राशि कें बिजली सेहो नहि पहुंचा सकय छै. हाई-वोल्टेज डीसी कनेक्शन, जेना कि बहारमपुर-भेरामरा मे, जखन बिजली कें एसी सं डीसी मे बदलल जायत छै, कियाकि इ ट्रांसमिशन लाइन कें साथ चलै छै, आ जखन रिसीविंग एंड पर वापस एसी मे बदलल जायत छै, तखन किछ बिजली कें नुकसान भ जायत छै. अभिनकर क अनुमान अछि जे 1 जीडब्ल्यू लाइन पर मोटा-मोटी 40-50 मेगावाट क नुकसान भ सकैत अछि। बहारमपुर-भेरामारा गलियारा भी भारत केरऽ खुद केरऽ बंगलादेश केरऽ निर्यात स॑ भरलऽ छै । भारत केरऽ केंद्रीय बिजली प्राधिकरण “अपनऽ तापीय सीमा के करीब लाइन क॑ नै चलाबै चाहै छै ... ऐन्हऽ लाइन प॑ जे भारत केरऽ अपनऽ द्विपक्षीय निर्यात भी ले जाय छै”, सेंटर फॉर साइंस एंड एनवायरनमेंट (सीएसई) केरऽ अक्षय ऊर्जा केरऽ डिप्टी प्रोग्राम मैनेजर बिनित दास न॑ नोट करलकै । अभिनकर आरू कहै छै कि भारत-बांग्लादेश लिंक लेली बैटरी स्टोरेज संभावित रूप स॑ मदद करी सकै छै अगर कम मांग के दौरान लाइन म॑ स्पेयर क्षमता छै । मुदा व्यवहार्यता एहि बात पर निर्भर करैत अछि जे इंटरकनेक्टेशन पर बिजलीक प्रवाह दिन भरि कतेक बदलैत रहैत अछि । राजनीति बिजली व्यापार के जटिल बनाबै छै भूगोल भारत के सामने कोनो भी भविष्य के नेपाल-बांग्लादेश विद्युत व्यापार में अपरिहार्य भूमिका के सामने पेश करै छै । भारत केरऽ कंज्यूमर यूनिटी एंड ट्रस्ट सोसाइटी (सीयूटीएस) केरऽ कार्यकारी निदेशक बिपुल चट्टोपाध्याय न॑ कहलकै कि भारत केरऽ सहायता के बिना बंगलादेश क॑ नेपाल या भूटान स॑ बिजली मिलै के दोसरऽ तरीका नै छै । विशेषज्ञ ई 20 मेगावाट केरऽ एपिसोड क॑ ई बात लेली लिटमस टेस्ट के रूप म॑ देखै छै कि भारत साझा संपत्ति केरऽ प्रतिस्पर्धी उपयोगऽ म॑ क्षमता क॑ कोना प्राथमिकता दै छै । एहि गतिरोध के दौरान भारत आ नेपाल अलग-अलग बहुत पैघ क्षमता वाला निर्णय पर पहुंचल छल जे नेपाल के निर्यात कोटा के 1.1 जीडब्ल्यू सं बढ़ा क 1.65 जीडब्ल्यू क देल जाए. सीएसई केरऽ दास न॑ कहलकै कि वू द्विपक्षीय फैसला कतनी जल्दी होय गेलै आरू त्रिपक्षीय २० मेगावाट कतनी देर स॑ सुस्त रहलऽ छै, ई बात के बीच के विषमता ही ई सबस॑ स्पष्ट सबूत छै कि ई क्षेत्र केरऽ एकीकरण के समस्या वास्तव म॑ कत॑ बैठलऽ छै । नेपाल के जलविद्युत क्षेत्र मे भारत के भूमिका सेहो तस्वीर के जटिल बना दैत अछि. नेपाल म॑ कईएक भारतीय कंपनी बड़ऽ जलविद्युत परियोजना विकसित करी रहलऽ छै, जबकि भारत नेपाल केरऽ प्रमुख बिजली निर्यात बाजार आरू बांग्लादेश म॑ निर्यात केरऽ पारगमन देश भी छै । चट्टोपाध्याय के कहनाय छनि जे भारत अपन बढ़ैत मांग के पूरा करय लेल नेपाल के जलविद्युत के तेजी सं फायदा उठा सकैत अछि. चुनौती इ छै कि एकटा एहन रूपरेखा तैयार कैल जै जे एहि मे शामिल सबटा देशक कें लेल काज करय. ओ कहैत छथि जे तीनू पार्टी कए इ जीत-जीत हेबाक चाही। “ओ मॉडल क॑ विकसित करना मुश्किल नै छै, लेकिन वू एगो ऐसनऽ चीज छै जे हमरऽ वर्तमान राजनीतिक-आर्थिक प्रवचन म॑ अखनी भी गायब छै।” ओ 20 मेगावाट क इनकार मे राजनीतिक विचार सेहो उठबैत छथि। अगस्त २०२४ म॑ बांग्लादेश केरऽ पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री शेख हसीना भारत म॑ निर्वासन होय ​​गेलऽ छेलै, तब॑ स॑ भारत आरू बांग्लादेश के बीच संबंध तनावपूर्ण छै, जहां हुनी अखनी भी छै । चट्टोपाध्याय नोट करै छै, “बंग्लादेश म॑ सरकार म॑ बदलाव के बाद [भारत-बांग्लादेश केरऽ] संबंध अभी सही रास्ता प॑ नै आबी सकलऽ छै ... ई बहुत ठंढा छै । दक्षिण एशियाई बिजली बाजार? महज 20 मेगावाट कें स्थानांतरित करय कें कठिनाई ऊर्जा कें जरूरत बढ़य वाला क्षेत्र मे सीमा पार सं ऊर्जा व्यापार मे अड़चन कें ओर इशारा करय छै. मूल 40 मेगावाट सहित संचरण गलियारा केरऽ हर पूर्व विस्तार क॑ संयुक्त संचालन समिति (जेएससी) केरऽ फैसला के माध्यम स॑ औपचारिक रूप देलऽ गेलऽ छेलै आरू ओकरऽ बाद त्रिपक्षीय समझौता करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । नेपाल-भारत जेएससीके १३म बैसार जुलाईमे भेल छल, जे अन्तिम बेर फरवरी २०२५मे बजाओल गेल छल, मुदा २० मेगावाटके जोडलासँ सफलता नहि भेट सकल । एकटा व्यापक संस्थागत समस्या सेहो अछि। बांग्लादेश, भूटान आरू नेपाल के बीच सीमा पार स॑ बिजली के व्यापार, जहां ई भारत स॑ गुजरै छै, ओकरा लेली कई परतऽ के मंजूरी के जरूरत छै । एहि मे त्रिपक्षीय बिजली बिक्री समझौता, भारत क केंद्रीय बिजली प्राधिकरण स मंजूरी आ एहि फैसला कए लंगर लगेबा लेल जेएससी शामिल अछि। पिछला किछु साल स बांग्लादेश, भूटान आ नेपाल भारत क संग बिजली व्यापार क विकास लेल द्विपक्षीय समझौता पर हस्ताक्षर केलक अछि। अप्रैल तक भारत पड़ोसी देशक संग 17 बिजली क्षेत्रक समझौता कएने अछि। इ सीमा पार सं 13 बिजली उत्पादन परियोजना आ 30 संचरण-लिंक परियोजना मे सेहो शामिल छै. दास कहैत छथि जे त्रिपक्षीय आ क्षेत्रीय लेनदेन मे राजनीतिक आ प्रक्रियात्मक घर्षण क परत होइत अछि जे द्विपक्षीय लेनदेन मे नहि होइत अछि । एहि सं एहि क्षेत्र के बिजली प्रणाली एक दोसरा सं जुड़ल अछि मुदा खंडित भ गेल अछि. गहन एकीकरण कें संभावित लाभ महत्वपूर्ण छै. सीयूटीएस आरू चिंतन रिसर्च फाउंडेशन केरऽ संयुक्त शोध म॑ पता चललै कि सीमा पार स॑ बिजली व्यापार ई देशऽ क॑ एक-दूसरा के मांग के पूरक बनाबै के अनुमति द॑ सकै छै, जेकरा स॑ जीवाश्म ईंधन प॑ निर्भरता कम होय सकै छै जबकि ऊर्जा सुरक्षा म॑ सुधार आरू लागत म॑ कमी ​​आबै छै । अलग-अलग आकार के देश के लेल सेहो दांव अलग-अलग अछि. अभिनकर कहै छै, "भारत जैसनऽ बड़ऽ सिस्टम लेली ... सीमा पार स॑ छोटऽ व्यापार स॑ वास्तव म॑ बहुत बड़ऽ फर्क नै पड़ै छै ।लेकिन नेपाल जैसनऽ देश लेली अपनऽ जलविद्युत बेचै लेली [आरू] बांग्लादेश जैसनऽ देश लेली अपनऽ बिजली के मांग क॑ भरोसेमंद तरीका स॑ पूरा करै लेली सीमा पार स॑ व्यापार महत्वपूर्ण होय जाय छै । तइयो एखन धरि कोनो उपक्षेत्रीय संस्था नहि अछि जे सीमा पार सं बिजली व्यापार के समन्वय आ सुविधा देबय पर केंद्रित अछि. दास के कहना छै कि क्षेत्रीय बिजली आदान-प्रदान, सहमत खुला पहुँच ढाँचा या संस्थागत, कैलेंडर स॑ जुड़लऽ त्रिपक्षीय निकाय तेसरऽ देशऽ के पारगमन क॑ संभाल॑ के अधिक पूर्वानुमानित तरीका उपलब्ध करै सकै छै । हुनी कहै छै, “बिना ऐसनौ तंत्र के 20 मेगावाट के होल्डअप जैसनऽ एपिसोड दोबारा आबी सकै छै, भले ही क्षेत्र केरऽ बढ़तऽ जलविद्युत अधिशेष आरू पूरक बिजली के मांग व्यापार केरऽ मामला क॑ तेजी स॑ स्पष्ट करी दै छै । ई लेख मूल रूप स॑ डायलॉग अर्थ प॑ क्रिएटिव कॉमन्स लाइसेंस के तहत प्रकाशित करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

title: Video showing Chinese survivor’s rescue in Nepal released - Korea JoongAng Daily
description: Video showing Chinese survivor’s rescue in Nepal released  Korea JoongAng Daily
publisher.title: Korea JoongAng Daily
full_article:
Video footage showing the tense moment when the Korea Disaster Relief Team (KDRT) rescued a Chinese survivor of the Nepal flash flood was released by Korean authorities on Sunday.

“Are you okay?” a Korean rescuer asked as they pointed the flashlight toward what appeared to be a human figure.

As Korean rescuers approached closer, they confirmed the survivor was waiting on a platform above the flood debris inside the tunnel.

Related Article Far from home, Nepali students in Korea grapple with tragedy of flood

Chinese ambassador thanks Korean rescuers after survivor found in Nepal floods

With the rescuers' instructions and assistance, the survivor climbed down from the platform on his own using an attached metal beam.

The survivor was wearing a full-sleeve T-shirt and only boxer shorts. He was not wearing shoes.

“When the rescuers’ light shone on me, I could not shout back because I could not believe that they were here to save me,” the survivor told Chinese broadcaster CCTV.

A Chinese survivor trapped inside a tunnel smiles as Korean rescuers come to save him in footage carried by Yonhap News TV. KOREA DISASTER RELIEF TEAM

The footage was recorded with a camera attached to the Korean rescuers' helmets. The clip also showed the rescuers wading through mud that reached their upper torsos.

The Chinese survivor was found inside a 225-meter-long (738-foot-long) tunnel and was later transported to a military hospital by helicopter.

The survivor was found at the hydropower plant construction site where the nine missing Koreans had been working. One Korean is believed to be near the weir dam, close to where the survivor was found, while the other eight are believed to be farther downstream.

The KDRT plans to continue the search mission inside the tunnel, as the survivor said another person was nearby, though he did not know whether the person was alive.

Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun is also set to hold ministerial talks with his Nepali counterpart regarding rescue efforts to find missing Koreans.





BY LEE SOO-JUNG [lee.soojung1@joongang.co.kr]
translated:
कोरिया आपदा राहत दल (केडीआरटी) न॑ नेपाल केरऽ झटका बाढ़ स॑ बची क॑ निकललऽ चीनी आदमी क॑ बचाबै के तनावपूर्ण क्षण क॑ देखाबै वाला वीडियो फुटेज रविवार क॑ कोरियाई अधिकारियऽ न॑ जारी करलकै ।

“अहाँ ठीक छी?” एकटा कोरियाई बचावकर्ता टॉर्च के ओहि दिस इशारा करैत पुछलकै जे मनुक्खक आकृति बुझाइत छल.

कोरियाई बचावकर्ता सब जेना-जेना नजदीक आबि रहल छल, ओ सब पुष्टि केलक जे बचि गेल आदमी सुरंग के अंदर बाढ़ के मलबा के ऊपर एकटा प्लेटफार्म पर इंतजार क रहल छल।

संबंधित लेख घर स दूर कोरिया मे नेपाली छात्र बाढ़िक त्रासदी स जूझैत छथि

नेपाल में बाढ़ि के 12 दिन बाद एखनो लापता 9 कोरियाई के खोज में चीनी बचि गेल चीनी के बचाओल गेल

नेपालक बाढ़िमे बचि गेल व्यक्ति भेटलाक बाद कोरियाई उद्धारकके धन्यवाद दैत चीनी राजदूत

लापता कोरियाई के खोज, अन्य बाढ़ के मुद्दा पर मन्त्री वार्ता के लेल विदेश मन्त्री नेपाल जेताह

बचावकर्मी के निर्देश आरू सहायता स॑ बची गेलऽ आदमी संलग्न धातु के बीम के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ अपनऽ दम प॑ प्लेटफार्म स॑ नीचें चढ़ी गेलै ।

बचि गेल व्यक्ति फुल स्लीव टी-शर्ट आ केवल बॉक्सर शॉर्ट्स पहिरने छल। जूता नहि पहिरने छलाह।

चीनी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी स बचि गेल व्यक्ति कहला जे जखन बचावकर्मी क इजोत हमरा पर चमकल त हम वापस चिचिया नहि सकलहुं, किया कि हमरा विश्वास नहि भ रहल छल जे ओ हमरा बचाबय लेल एतय आयल छथि।

सुरंग के भीतर फंसलऽ एगो चीनी बची गेलऽ आदमी मुस्कुराबै छै जब॑ कोरियाई बचावकर्मी ओकरा बचाबै लेली आबै छै, जेकरा म॑ योनहाप न्यूज टीवी द्वारा देलऽ गेलऽ फुटेज छै । कोरिया आपदा राहत टीम

चीनी बची गेलऽ ई व्यक्ति क॑ २२५ मीटर (७३८ फीट लंबा) सुरंग के भीतर मिललै आरू बाद म॑ ओकरा हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ सैन्य अस्पताल पहुँचैलऽ गेलै ।

बचि गेल व्यक्ति जलविद्युत संयंत्र निर्माण स्थल पर भेटल जतय नौ टा लापता कोरियाई काज क रहल छल। मानल जा रहल अछि जे एकटा कोरियाई वेयर डैम के पास अछि, जतय सं बचल बच्चा भेटल छल, ओकर नजदीक अछि, जखन कि बाकी आठ गोटे के बारे में मानल जा रहल अछि जे ओ बेसी नीचा अछि.

केडीआरटी केरऽ योजना छै कि सुरंग के भीतर खोज मिशन जारी रखलऽ जाय, कैन्हेंकि बची गेलऽ आदमी न॑ कहलकै कि पास म॑ एगो आरू व्यक्ति छै, हालांकि ओकरा ई पता नै छेलै कि वू व्यक्ति जीवित छै कि नै ।

कोरिया केरऽ विदेश मंत्री चो ह्यून न॑ भी लापता कोरियाई लोगऽ क॑ खोजै के बचाव के प्रयास के संबंध म॑ अपनऽ नेपाली समकक्ष के साथ मन्त्री वार्ता करै वाला छै ।

title: Nepali community rallies for flood victims in West Hartford - NBC Connecticut
description: Nepali community rallies for flood victims in West Hartford  NBC Connecticut
publisher.title: NBC Connecticut
full_article:
The Nepali community gathered Sunday in West Hartford to mourn the victims of devastating floods in Nepal and raise money for relief efforts more than a week after the disaster.

More than 1,300 people have died and more than 5,000 remain missing across Nepal and China after flooding that was likely triggered by a glacier collapse.

Stream Connecticut News for free, 24/7, wherever you are. WATCH HERE

In West Hartford, community members lit candles and arranged them around the flag of Nepal during a vigil for those affected by the disaster.

“We’re sending prayers and hoping they’re okay,” 14-year-old Kashvi Kandeo of West Hartford said.

The flooding swept away buildings and people, leaving members of Connecticut’s Nepali community struggling to comprehend videos showing the destruction.

“It really hurts to see your home country get destroyed like this,” Kandeo said.

That shock has also prompted the community to take action. The vigil brought together members of the Nepali community as well as local and state leaders while raising money for relief efforts.

Local South Windsor 3 hours ago Crews search for missing male after jet ski accident West Haven 10 hours ago Suspect bit police K-9 while being apprehended by officers in West Haven: police

“Whenever these things happen, the whole community comes together and want to gather and try to support it,” West Hartford resident Pramod Pradhan said.

West Hartford is home to one of Connecticut’s largest Nepali communities, with about 1,000 Nepali people living in Hartford County, based on data compiled by the Asian and Asian American Studies Institute at UConn.

Vigil organizers said they have collectively raised a few thousand dollars to support relief efforts.

Community members said the disaster has also demonstrated the resilience of the Nepali people.

“They’re really strong for that because so much has happened and the fact that they can keep pushing forward it just really shows how strong they are,” Kandeo said.

Organizers in West Hartford are asking people who want to contribute to relief efforts in Nepal to donate directly to the Nepalese government. That can be found here.

title: A local woman is finding ways to help family and community back in Nepal - kimt.com
description: A local woman is finding ways to help family and community back in Nepal  kimt.com
publisher.title: kimt.com
full_article:
MINNEAPOLIS (WCCO) -- For Jeena Gurung Vomhof, the Minnesota State Fair was supposed to be a celebration.

A chance to share the art and traditions of the country she still calls home.

Then came devastating news from Nepal.

"I was almost done with the set up to be selling at the 2026 Minnesota State Fair. Excited, pumped, you know, new space, new energy, and I couldn't, I couldn't see my social media, like what's happening. It was like, that was not real to me. And I just called my mom and said what's happening," said Gurung Vomhof.

Gurung Vomhof is originally from Kathmandu.

Nepal is home to Gurung Vomhof's family, her memories, and the women whose work she brings to Minnesota.

"Nepal is a beautiful country. It's an Asian country, right below China and above India, surrounded by beautiful mountains, beautiful people, the tradition, the culture, the love, the humanity that is there in the country I still miss and I try to bring that wherever I go," explained Gurung Vomhof.

Through her business, Namaste Brows & Boutique in Roseville, Gurung Vomhof employs sixteen women in Nepalmaking — hand-crafted earrings, cashmere shawls, hemp, and felt gift items. 100% of the proceeds go back to the makers.

"Each and every piece that I sell has a story," said Gurung Vomhof.

But right now, she's carrying a story of loss.

"My friends, my family, who are far and close, are still back home and we have lost two cousins, 21 and 35, who were going trekking. They're missing," said Gurung Vomhof.

She talks with family every day, trying to stay connected while holding herself together.

At the fair, people she doesn't know are giving her something she needs right now.

"My favorite thing right now is hugs. You know, when I'm holding all of this, I don't know how, I have the right word physically, emotionally. Joy, hurt? That hug means so much," said Gurung Vomhof

Those moments are helping her keep going.

She's already thinking beyond the immediate crisis - about children, education, and rebuilding.

"Education is the root of everything, everything. For me, maybe I can build a classroom, but I can't do it alone. I need all of you," said Gurung Vomhof.

For now, she'll keep standing for Nepal, sharing its culture, and believing in the people standing with her.

"I am at the grandstand at the lower level, row number nine, wide open with colors, with joy, and I'm going to be standing here every single minute," said Gurung Vomhof.
