title: Monday Starter: Nun leading Caritas Nepal calls for international aid after floods - Global Sisters Report
description: Monday Starter: Nun leading Caritas Nepal calls for international aid after floods  Global Sisters Report
publisher.title: Global Sisters Report
full_article:
With the death toll mounting to more than 1,000 and with more than 4,500 missing, the executive director of Caritas Nepal is warning that the disaster caused by massive flooding in the country on Aug. 26 has not fully played out and will require international support for months to come. "The situation remains extremely alarming, and the number of casualties continues to rise as search and rescue operations are still ongoing," Sr. Cecilia Durga Shrestha, a member of the Sisters of St. Joseph of Cluny and head of Caritas Nepal since 2023, said of Nepal government search, rescue and relief efforts. "Thousands of people have been affected, with many lives lost, people still missing, and significant damage to homes, roads, bridges, livelihoods and other essential infrastructure," Shrestha told GSR, speaking specifically of the flooding that swept through communities in Nuwakot near the Himalayan nation's border with China.

Sr. Cecilia Durga Shrestha, a member of the Sisters of St. Joseph of Cluny, has been serving as executive director of Caritas Nepal since 2023. (Courtesy of Caritas Nepal)

Shrestha said that since the second day of the disaster, Caritas Nepal and its partners have been on the ground accompanying affected communities. "We are providing food and non-food items, essential household utensils, and other emergency supplies," Shrestha said. "We are also supporting people who have lost family members with essential items needed for mourning and funeral rituals, as well as providing medical kits to affected communities in different locations." However, at present, the most urgent needs include temporary shelter, debris clearance, essential household items, temporary learning centers for children, psychosocial counseling, medical assistance and support to restore basic livelihoods and services. Shrestha stressed the need for the international community to continue accompanying affected communities in the coming months. "Financial support would be particularly valuable to enable us to respond to both immediate humanitarian needs and the longer-term recovery and rebuilding of affected families and communities," she said. Nepal has a population of 31 million and is predominantly Hindu, with only about 10,000 Roman Catholics. But Caritas' response, Shrestha said, is to extend a "helping hand to the affected people from the ground," regardless of religious affiliation.

Loyola University honors the late Sr. Jean Schmidt with campus statue Loyola University Chicago has honored one of its icons, the late Sr. Jean Dolores Schmidt — longtime Loyola Ramblers basketball fan, team chaplain and campus fixture — with a statue on the university's Rogers Park campus. The Aug. 21 unveiling of the cast bronze statue, which depicts Schmidt sitting on a bench and holding a Loyola basketball, fell on what would have been the beloved sister's 107th birthday and a little less than a year since Schmidt's death at age 106 on Oct. 9, 2025. Known to all as Sister Jean, Schmidt received international attention and acclaim during the Loyola Ramblers' appearance during the 2018 NCAA March Madness tournament, the year she served as the team's chaplain at age 98.

Tom Hitcho, Loyola senior associate athletics director and longtime friend of Sr. Jean Schmidt, was the first to sit next to the statue after it was unveiled Aug. 21, 2026, at Loyola University Chicago. (Courtesy of Loyola University Chicago)

But during the statue unveiling ceremony, university officials and members of her congregation, the Sisters of Charity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, praised Schmidt for being more than a dedicated basketball fan. "Sister Jean's ministry of presence was a gift to generations of Ramblers," said Loyola President Mark Reed, who praised Schmidt's compassion, joy and concern and care for students and staff. In her remarks, Sr. LaDonna Manternach, president of the Sisters of Charity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, recalled Schmidt's love of Loyola students. "A good listener, she inspired many to pursue their dreams with purpose. Her deep trust in God guided her life and encouraged others to trust their own journey. "

एक हजार स बेसी मृतक आ 4500 स बेसी लापता भेला स कैरिटास नेपाल क कार्यकारी निदेशक चेतावनी द रहल छथि जे 26 अगस्त कए देश मे भारी बाढ़ि स भेल आपदा पूरा नहि भेल अछि आ आगामी महीनो तक अंतरराष्ट्रीय सहयोग क जरूरत पड़त। नेपाल सरकार के खोज, बचाव आरू राहत के प्रयास के बारे म॑ २०२३ स॑ क्लूनी केरऽ सेंट जोसेफ केरऽ सिस्टर्स केरऽ सदस्य आरू कैरिटास नेपाल केरऽ प्रमुख सीनियर सेसिलिया दुर्गा श्रेष्ठ न॑ कहलकै कि स्थिति अत्यंत चिंताजनक बनलऽ छै, आरू हताहतऽ के संख्या बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि खोज-बचाव केरऽ काम अखनी भी जारी छै । चीन के साथ हिमालयी राष्ट्र के सीमा के पास नुवाकोट मँ समुदायौ मँ बहलौ बाढ़ के बारे मँ विशेष रूप सँ बात करतें हुअय श्रेष्ठ नँ जीएसआर क बतैलकै कि हजारों लोग प्रभावित होय गेलौ छै, जेकरा मँ बहुत लोगौ के जान गेलौ छै, लोग अभी भी लापता छै, आरू घर, सड़क, पुल, आजीविका आरू अन्य आवश्यक बुनियादी ढाँचा क काफी नुकसान पहुँचैलौ गेलौ छै ।

क्लुनी के सेंट जोसेफ के सिस्टर्स के सदस्य सीनियर सेसिलिया दुर्गा श्रेष्ठ 2023 स कैरिटास नेपाल के कार्यकारी निदेशक के रूप में कार्यरत छैथ।(कैरिटास नेपाल के सौजन्य स)

श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, आपदा के दोसर दिन सं कैरिटास नेपाल आ ओकर साझेदार प्रभावित समुदाय के संग जमीन पर अछि। श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, हम खाद्य आ गैर खाद्य सामग्री, आवश्यक घरेलू बर्तन, आ अन्य आपातकालीन सामान उपलब्ध करा रहल छी। "हम शोक आरू अंतिम संस्कार के संस्कार लेली जरूरी आवश्यक सामान के साथ परिवार के सदस्यौ क गंवा चुकलौ लोगौ के साथ भी सहयोग करी रहलौ छियै, साथ ही अलग-अलग स्थान प प्रभावित समुदायौ क मेडिकल किट भी उपलब्ध करौ रहलौ छियै।" मुदा वर्तमान मे सब सं जरूरी जरूरतक मे अस्थायी आश्रय, मलबा निकासी, आवश्यक घरेलू सामान, बच्चाक कें लेल अस्थायी सीखय कें केंद्र, मनोसामाजिक परामर्श, चिकित्सा सहायता आ बुनियादी आजीविका आ सेवाक कें बहाल करय कें लेल सहायता शामिल छै. श्रेष्ठ आगामी महिनामे अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय समुदायके प्रभावित समुदायके साथ जारी राखैके आवश्यकतापर जोड देलक । हुनी कहलकै कि आर्थिक सहायता विशेष रूप स॑ मूल्यवान होतै ताकि हम्मं॑ तत्काल मानवीय जरूरत आरू प्रभावित परिवार आरू समुदाय केरऽ दीर्घकालिक वसूली आरू पुनर्निर्माण दूनू के जवाब द॑ सकियै । नेपालक जनसंख्या ३.१ करोड़ अछि आ हिन्दू प्रमुख अछि, मात्र लगभग १०,००० रोमन कैथोलिक अछि । लेकिन श्रेष्ठ न॑ कहलकै कि कैरिटास केरऽ प्रतिक्रिया ई छै कि “जमीन स॑ प्रभावित लोगऽ क॑ मदद करै के हाथ” बढ़ाबै के छै, चाहे वू धार्मिक संबद्धता के कोय भी होय ।

संबंधित : नेपालक बाढ़ि मे 'किछु नहि' छोड़ि गेल अछि, कारण कैथोलिक नन सभ सहायता जुटा रहल छथि

लोयोला विश्वविद्यालय न॑ कैंपस केरऽ मूर्ति स॑ स्वर्गीय सीनियर जीन श्मिट क॑ सम्मानित करलकै लोयोला यूनिवर्सिटी शिकागो न॑ अपनऽ एगो आइकन, स्वर्गीय सीनियर जीन डोलोरेस श्मिट — लंबा समय स॑ लोयोला रैम्बल्स केरऽ बास्केटबॉल प्रशंसक, टीम केरऽ चपरासी आरू कैंपस फिक्सचर — क॑ विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ रोजर्स पार्क परिसर म॑ एगो मूर्ति के साथ सम्मानित करलकै । 21 अगस्त कए कास्ट कांस्य मूर्ति क अनावरण, जाहि मे श्मिट कए बेंच पर बैसल आ लोयोला बास्केटबॉल पकड़ने देखाउल गेल अछि, जे प्रिय बहिन क 107म जन्मदिन आ 9 अक्टूबर 2025 कए 106 साल क उम्र मे श्मिट क निधन क एक साल स किछु कम समय पर पड़ल 2018 एनसीएए मार्च मैडनेस टूर्नामेंट के दौरान लोयोला रैम्बलर्स केरऽ उपस्थिति के दौरान ध्यान आरू प्रशंसा, जेकरा म॑ हुनी 98 साल के उम्र म॑ टीम केरऽ चपरासी के रूप म॑ काम करलकै ।

लोयोला केरऽ सीनियर एसोसिएट एथलेटिक्स डायरेक्टर आरू सीनियर जीन श्मिट केरऽ लंबा समय स॑ दोस्त टॉम हित्चो न॑ २१ अगस्त २०२६ क॑ लोयोला यूनिवर्सिटी शिकागो म॑ एकरऽ अनावरण के बाद सबसें पहलऽ मूर्ति के बगल म॑ बैठलऽ छेलै । (लोयोला विश्वविद्यालय शिकागो के सौजन्य)

लेकिन मूर्ति के अनावरण समारोह के दौरान विश्वविद्यालय के अधिकारी आरू हुनकऽ मंडली के सदस्य, सिस्टर्स ऑफ चैरिटी ऑफ द ब्लेसड वर्जिन मैरी न॑ श्मिट के प्रशंसा करलकै कि हुनी एगो समर्पित बास्केटबॉल प्रशंसक स॑ भी अधिक छै । लोयोला केरऽ अध्यक्ष मार्क रीड न॑ कहलकै कि सिस्टर जीन केरऽ उपस्थिति मंत्रालय रैम्बलर केरऽ पीढ़ी लेली एगो उपहार छेलै, जेकरा न॑ श्मिट केरऽ करुणा, खुशी आरू चिंता आरू छात्र आरू कर्मचारी केरऽ देखभाल के प्रशंसा करलकै । अपनऽ टिप्पणी म॑ सिस्टर्स ऑफ चैरिटी ऑफ द ब्लेसड वर्जिन मैरी केरऽ अध्यक्ष सीनियर लाडोना मंटरनच न॑ श्मिट केरऽ लोयोला केरऽ छात्रऽ के प्रति प्रेम के याद करलकै । "एकटा नीक श्रोता, ओ बहुतो केँ अपन सपना केँ उद्देश्य सँ पूरा करबाक लेल प्रेरित केलनि। भगवान पर हुनकर गहींर भरोसा हुनकर जीवन केँ मार्गदर्शन केलक आ दोसरो केँ अपन यात्रा पर भरोसा करबाक लेल प्रोत्साहित केलक।"

title: Nepal floods: Death toll climbs to 1,355 as rescue efforts continue; nearly 5,000 still missing - The Hindu
description: Nepal floods: Death toll climbs to 1,355 as rescue efforts continue; nearly 5,000 still missing  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal surged to 1,355 on Monday (September 7, 2026) as more bodies were recovered from the affected areas, authorities said.

Rescue teams continued to search for 4,996 people, including at least 589 foreign nationals, who remain missing, while 13,396 people have been rescued so far, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said.

Nepal flash floods: Death toll rises to 1,344

According to NDRRMA, 363 bodies have been recovered from Chitwan district, 221 from Nawalparasi West, 222 from Nawalparasi East and 197 from Nuwakot.

Similarly, 169 bodies were recovered from Rasuwa, 75 from Gorkha, 70 from Dhading and 38 from Tanahu, it said.

The joint command of security forces is actively conducting search and rescue operations.

Major rescue operations are underway at hydropower projects in flood-affected districts, where hundreds of men are believed to be trapped in tunnels. Teams of experts from India and China are assisting their Nepali counterparts in these operations.

The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.

Nepal flash floods 2026 Nepal observes national mourning on 13th day of flash flood tragedy

Nepal flood survivors join rescue and relief operations as they grieve, search for their loved ones

How a mountain collapse triggered Nepal’s deadly flood in just 7 minutes | The Climate Economy

Nepal floods: DNA testing offers last hope to families searching for missing loved ones

The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.

The disaster also killed at least 21 people on the Chinese side, while more than 500 people remain missing in Tibet, according to Chinese media reports.

title: Nepal mourns flood victims as hopes persist for workers trapped in tunnels - TRT World
description: Nepal mourns flood victims as hopes persist for workers trapped in tunnels  TRT World
publisher.title: TRT World
full_article:
Nepal held a national day of mourning on Monday for victims of devastating glacial floods, as families of missing hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels prayed rescuers might yet find them alive.

The August 26 glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,398 people, with more than 5,500 missing, including around 800 foreigners.

Flags flew at half-mast, with candlelight vigils planned later in the day, following traditional Hindu mourning rituals on the 13th day after death.

Hundreds of hydropower workers are among the missing, but the rescue of three of them from deep inside tunnels, two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday, have buoyed hopes that more could still be alive.

Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP on Monday that rescue efforts were continuing "with the same tempo we had on day one".

"Our focus is on search and rescue at three levels, on ground, by air, and in the tunnels," he said.

"We are making sure that no one is still stranded."

Entire communities have been swept away, roads destroyed, and homes demolished.

'Hope'

But families of some of the missing workers who gathered in the capital Kathmandu said the government must move faster.

"We have a lot of hope," said Reena Amatya Shrestha, whose brother is among the missing.

"They say they are doing rescue. If the rescue is there, where's the result? We need the result."

Related TRT World - Rescuers pull Chinese national alive from Nepal tunnel after 10 days

Australian tunnel rescue expert Arnold Dix, who is advising Nepali teams, said the operation presented an unprecedented challenge.

"We are facing something I have never faced before," said Dix, president of the International Tunnelling and Underground Space Association, in a post on social media.

"Not one rescue, but multiple potential rescues, unfolding at the same time, in different places, each with its own dangers, uncertainties, and lives that may still be saved."

नेपाल सेना के प्रवक्ता राजा राम बस्नेट सोमदिन एएफपी के कहलनि जे, बचाव के प्रयास जारी अछि, जेना पहिल दिन छल।

ओ कहला जे हमर ध्यान तीन स्तर पर, जमीन पर, हवाई मार्ग स आ सुरंग मे खोज आ बचाव पर अछि।

"हम सब ई सुनिश्चित क' रहल छी जे एखनो कियो फंसल नहि अछि।"

पूरा समुदाय बहल अछि, सड़क तबाह भ गेल अछि, आ घर तोड़ि देल गेल अछि।

'आशा'।

title: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer - Yahoo
description: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer  Yahoo
publisher.title: Yahoo
full_article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Some villages in Nepal have been so completely devastated by the floods that there is no sign they ever existed, according to Malaysian relief volunteers who have seen the destruction first-hand.

Mercy Malaysia Rapid Assessment Team leader Vivegananthan Rajangam said some settlements along the rivers were left without a single house after the floods tore through Benighat, Nuwakot and Bidur.

"The damage is very severe. In some villages, there isn't even one house left. If someone went there for the first time, they would think there was no village there," he told Harian Metro today.

"In many places hit by the floods along the river, nobody lives there anymore. In some places, there is no trace of any houses at all."

Even concrete buildings were not spared, with only about 20 per cent of such structures still standing in some settlements, he said.

"Most of these concrete buildings were also swept away," Vivegananthan recounted.

Survivors have since been moved away from the worst-hit areas, with many evacuated to Kathmandu and Nuwakot and housed in schools and halls on higher ground.

Vivegananthan said the Nepali authorities had also set up temporary shelters for those who survived the floods.

In Nuwakot alone, 19 such shelters have been established, he said.

Based on discussions with local authorities and assessments on the ground, food supplies at the shelters were adequate, but survivors needed other forms of assistance.

Mercy Malaysia's three-member team will remain in Nepal for about 10 days to assess how best to support those who survived the disaster.

Vivegananthan stressed that the team was not involved in search and rescue operations but was focused on helping survivors rebuild their lives.

"We are not involved in search and rescue. We are here to help those who survived," he said.

Among the assistance provided are medicines, cooking equipment and toys for children, which are being channelled through Nepali authorities, including the country's Health Ministry.

"The assistance we provide is aimed at helping them continue their lives as best as possible so they can return to normal," Vivegananthan said.

title: Virginia group raises money and awareness for Nepal after catastrophic flooding - WTOP News
description: Virginia group raises money and awareness for Nepal after catastrophic flooding  WTOP News
publisher.title: WTOP News
full_article:
Eleven days after catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border killed more than 1,300 people and left thousands missing, hundreds of workers are still believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites buried by mudslides.

Former Haymarket Town Council member Madhu Panthi and the Manassas-based America Nepal Helping Society are asking for support.

“In the world, I’d like to humbly request if there is any equipment that can dig and to open the tunnel … you know more than 5,000 people are missing. And what is the best mechanism to save their life? That’s what we are looking for,” Panthi said.

Panthi moved to Northern Virginia from Nepal in 2001 and helped coordinate donations and disaster response efforts after a 7.8 magnitude earthquake killed thousands and damaged more than 1 million homes and buildings in Nepal in 2015.

“That earthquake also did lots of damage. But earthquake, you can remove the debris and you can find the people in there. But this one is, you know, wiping out everything, and now the roads are not there. The bridges are not there. House, school and everything, everything is destroyed and wiped away,” Panthi said

The nonprofit has set an initial goal of raising $100,000 to support emergency shelter, food, water, health services and other relief efforts. As of Sunday, it had raised more than $52,000.

Panthi said the group is working with the Embassy of Nepal in D.C. and the Nepalese government, to help determine where the money is needed most.

According to the organization’s website, all donations are “subject to due diligence and final approval” and that the money “may support Government of Nepal disaster-relief funds identified in the Government’s 26 August appeal and/or other qualified humanitarian recipients.”

“They can donate by credit card. They can send by check. And all money goes 100% to the victims of Nepal: their food, their shelter, their medical, you know, their clothes, their livelihood,” Panthi said.

Panthi, who said one of his closest friends remains among the missing, told WTOP that ANHS is not sending rescue teams to the disaster area, unlike after Nepal’s 2015 earthquake when some of the group’s members went to distribute aid alongside Fairfax County Fire and Rescue personnel deployed with USAID’s Disaster Assistance Response Team.

Instead, the group is focused on raising money and working within Nepal’s “one door policy,” which is intended to streamline relief distribution and prevent aid from being unevenly distributed. “We don’t want to, you know, send somebody and then some area-people are not getting [help], and some area-people have too much,” Panthi said.

Panthi said that’s another reason ANHS is so focused on its financial goal to help Nepal: “Our heart, our brain, our everything is there. Our family are there. What can we do?”

Last week, PKP Tender Hearts Foundation, an area group dedicated to preserving Nepalese culture and serving communities in Nepal, held a candlelight vigil in Fairfax County with the George Mason University’s Nepalese Student Association to raise money and awareness for the flood victims.

People interested in donating to the America Nepal Helping Society’s disaster relief fund can do so through the organization’s website.

गैर-लाभकारी संगठन न॑ आपातकालीन आश्रय, भोजन, पानी, स्वास्थ्य सेवा आरू अन्य राहत प्रयासऽ म॑ सहायता लेली एक लाख डॉलर जुटाबै के प्रारंभिक लक्ष्य तय करल॑ छै । रविदिन तक एहि स 52 हजार डॉलर स बेसी क राशि जुटा चुकल छल।

पंथी कहलनि जे, समूह डी.सी.मे नेपालक दूतावास आ नेपाल सरकारक संग मिलिकय, ई निर्धारित करबा मे मदद क’ रहल अछि जे एहि पाइक बेसी आवश्यकता कतय अछि।

संगठन केरऽ वेबसाइट के अनुसार, सब दान “यथोचित परिश्रम आरू अंतिम मंजूरी के अधीन” छै आरू ई पैसा “सरकार केरऽ २६ अगस्त केरऽ अपील म॑ चिन्हित नेपाल सरकार केरऽ आपदा-राहत कोष आरू/या अन्य योग्य मानवीय प्राप्तकर्ता केरऽ समर्थन करी सकै छै ।”

"क्रेडिट कार्डसँ दान दऽ सकैए। चेकसँ पठा सकैए। आ सभटा पाइ शत-प्रतिशत नेपालक पीड़ितकेँ जाइत अछि: ओकर भोजन, ओकर आवास, ओकर मेडिकल, अहाँकेँ बुझल अछि, ओकर कपड़ा, ओकर रोजी-रोटी।'

पंथी, जे कहलकै कि हुनकऽ एगो करीबी दोस्त लापता लोगऽ म॑ शामिल छै, न॑ डब्ल्यूटीओपी क॑ बतैलकै कि एएनएचएस आपदा क्षेत्र म॑ बचाव दल नै भेज॑ रहलऽ छै, जेना कि नेपाल म॑ २०१५ केरऽ भूकंप के बाद समूह केरऽ कुछ सदस्य यूएसएआईडी केरऽ आपदा सहायता प्रतिक्रिया टीम के साथ तैनात फेयरफैक्स काउंटी फायर एंड रेस्क्यू कर्मी के साथ सहायता वितरित करै लेली गेलऽ छेलै ।

बल्कि ई समूह पैसा जुटाबै आरू नेपाल केरऽ “एक दरवाजा नीति” के भीतर काम करै प॑ केंद्रित छै, जेकरऽ उद्देश्य राहत वितरण क॑ सुव्यवस्थित करै आरू सहायता केरऽ असमान वितरण नै होय छै । पंथी कहलनि, “हमरा लोकनि नहि चाहैत छी, अहाँ केँ बुझल अछि, ककरो पठाबी आ तखन किछु एरिया-लोक केँ [मदद] नहि भेटि रहल छैक, आ किछु एरिया-लोक केँ बेसी छैक.”

पंथी कहलनि जे, एएनएचएस नेपाल के मदद के लेल अपन आर्थिक लक्ष्य पर एतेक ध्यान केंद्रित करबाक एकटा आओर कारण अछि: “हमर दिल, हमर दिमाग, हमर सब किछु अछि. हमर परिवार ओतय अछि. हम सब की क’ सकैत छी?”

पिछला सप्ताह नेपाली संस्कृति के संरक्षण आ नेपाल के समुदाय के सेवा के लेल समर्पित क्षेत्रीय समूह पीकेपी टेंडर हार्टस फाउंडेशन जॉर्ज मेसन विश्वविद्यालय के नेपाली छात्र संघ के संग फेयरफैक्स काउंटी में मोमबत्ती के रोशनी में जागरण क बाढ़ पीड़ित के लेल पैसा आ जागरूकता पैदा केलक।

अमेरिका नेपाल हेल्पिंग सोसाइटी के आपदा राहत कोष में दान देबय के इच्छुक लोक संस्था के वेबसाइट के माध्यम सं दान क सकय छथिन्ह.

एहि ठाम साइन अप करि अपन ईमेल इनबॉक्स मे ब्रेकिंग न्यूज आओर दैनिक हेडलाइन पहुंचाउ.

title: China Falls Victim To Own Secrecy After Nepal’s Deadly Floods - Newsweek
description: China Falls Victim To Own Secrecy After Nepal’s Deadly Floods  Newsweek
publisher.title: Newsweek
full_article:
China finds itself fighting an information war over its strategic interests in the Himalayas after last month’s devastating flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border put a spotlight on a major hydropower megaproject near India—over 600 miles away and still shrouded in secrecy.

Flooding triggered by a glacial collapse on August 26 claimed over 1,300 lives and up to four times that are still missing, including dozens of Americans. The U.S. Geological Survey said the Lhenda and Trishuli rivers carried glacial debris—ice, water, boulders and later rubble—approximately 62 miles downslope into central Nepal.

China has no hydropower stations upstream, and its infrastructure projects could have played no part in the ice avalanche, the latest assessments suggest. But China is the main contributor of civil engineering works along the riverbanks, so experts speculate that its bridges, highways and buildings in the valley may have altered the speed and composition of the debris flow.

Read More on World

While China and its neighbor India vie for influence over Nepal, Beijing’s skeptics in New Delhi say the worst disaster of its kind in the Himalayas should serve as a warning about Chinese hydropower plans elsewhere in Tibet and their effects downstream. China is fighting back.

When Disaster Strikes

Preliminary reports aided by satellite imagery said the landslide likely began at an elevation of over 17,000 feet, on the northern slope of the Langtang Lirung mountain in Nepal. The collapsing glacier crashed into the valley floor at such a force that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 earthquake, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

The first images of the torrent of mud and floodwater came from surveillance cameras at China’s Gyirong port, which was washed away in a matter of seconds. The border crossing was the main land route for China’s trade with Nepal.

For those living and working in the path of the floods, what little forewarning there was had come too late. Satellite imagery provided by Planet showed the destruction left behind by the fast-moving floodwater, like a giant scar in the earth.

...

When disaster strikes, Beijing’s first reaction is containment, of the damage but also of information.

Within hours of the flooding, videos filmed by witnesses were censored on Chinese social media apps almost as quickly as they were being uploaded. Only approved state media footage remained, as well as any videos that made it out of China’s Great Firewall.

It took the Chinese government 11 days to permit foreign media to report from the Gyirong border area. Beijing’s intense need for control created an informative vacuum in which unfavorable narratives bloomed.

One widely quoted statement came from Madhav Prasad Chaulagain, the former Nepalese environment minister, who said China had failed to warn Nepal about the floods. The comments made to an Indian broadcaster fed critics for days over Beijing’s alleged reluctance to share hydrological data.

Nepalese officials sought environmental monitoring data from Chinese counterparts—including on glacier-related hazards—three months before the disaster but never received it, Reuters reported.

"The broader lesson for the rest of the world is that China’s censorship and cover-ups should not be dismissed as problems affecting only the Chinese people. Opacity does not stay within national borders. Sooner or later, people elsewhere may also bear the costs," Henry Gao, a professor of law at Singapore Management University, said on X.

"The international community should press China to become more transparent and accountable. But meaningful accountability will remain elusive unless China undertakes fundamental political reform and becomes a democracy," Gao said.

China controls the rivers upstream, and water level information can be considered strategically sensitive. Nepal says it will rebuild an early warning system on its border with China utilizing sensors and cameras, but there’s every chance its neighbor will push back.

After Indian and Nepalese social media users on X said China’s lack of transparency was to blame for the deadly floods, the Chinese embassy in Kathmandu fired back, saying the allegations were designed to disrupt China’s cooperation with Nepal.

Chinese authorities, responding to concerns about an information blackout that could cost lives, said they were already sharing whatever data they had. China’s state broadcaster CCTV said glaciers often move and were difficult to predict before collapse.

...

The Himalayas are warming at twice the global average, experts say, making it vulnerable to environmental catastrophes including landslides and floods.

Last week, the Chinese ambassador to Nepal, Zhang Maoming, shared an op-ed written by a Chinese professor in the government-owned newspaper Rising Nepal Daily , which shifted blame for the disaster onto the West.

"The warming in Nepal and the Tibetan Plateau isn't the result of local emissions—it's the accumulated, centuries-old carbon emissions of the industrialized Global North that are bearing down on a cryosphere both countries depend on for their water security," it said.

The Damage Is Done

China’s leaders know the dangers of a runaway narrative, about a palace coup or the instability of the Communist Party’s rule. Its censorship was only partly to do with not wanting to look bad.

Externally, Beijing would’ve been aware of what the disaster meant for its role as a reliable economic partner to Nepal and other developing countries. Internally, its response would speak to its ability to safely manage the region of Tibet, a source of tension with New Delhi, which has hosted the 14th Dalai Lama in exile in northern India for nearly seven decades.

China’s preference for secrecy, however, could cause the greatest damage to its interests in eastern Tibet, where it’s building the world’s largest dam on a river that sustains tens of millions of lives downstream.

The Medog hydropower project, which began last year and will run into the 2030s, will solidify Chinese control of the Yarlung Tsangpo, the critical freshwater source of the Brahmaputra in India and later the Jamuna in Bangladesh.

Nearly a dozen dams of varying sizes have already been built in the eastern parts of politically sensitive Tibet, a geologically fragile region known for devastating earthquakes in the past.

"The geological danger is only part of the story. China is increasingly transforming its control of the Tibetan Plateau—the source of most of Asia’s major rivers—into strategic leverage," Brahma Chellaney, a professor of strategic studies at the Center for Policy Research, a New Delhi think tank, said in an analysis written before the glacial collapse in Nepal.

"It has built cascades of dams on transboundary rivers, withheld hydrological data during periods of tension, and resisted entering any water-sharing treaty with downstream states. Water has become another instrument of coercive statecraft," Chellaney said.

The Chinese government has invited additional scrutiny of its "project of the century" because it won’t disclose further details about the scale of the super dam.

"A secretive Chinese project in my eyes means it’s hard for anyone to find credible information about it, even in Chinese. That is the case for the now under-construction hydropower mega-project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River in eastern Tibet," Shanghai-based energy analyst David Fishman said in a recent Substack newsletter.

China says the $170 billion dam will generate 60 gigawatts of electricity, three times that of the Three Gorges Dam in central China—the largest hydropower facility in the world.

"Yet for all the fanfare about the project’s ambitious scale, the public knows very little about what kind of facility it even is, never mind details like the construction milestones, power export destinations, effects on the surrounding environment, or expected impact on human populations," Fishman said.

Since the disaster in Nepal, Indian social media users on X and other commentators have described China’s mega dam as a "time bomb" that could threaten India.

China may disagree but its reluctance to share information means it’s letting others control the narrative.

Mutual trust in the contested Himalayas is low, and it’s about to get lower.

चीन हिमालय म॑ अपनऽ सामरिक हित के चलतें सूचना युद्ध लड़ै वाला पाबै छै, कैन्हेंकि पिछला महीना नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा प॑ विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ न॑ भारत के पास एगो बड़ऽ जलविद्युत मेगाप्रोजेक्ट प॑ प्रकाश डाललकै-600 मील स॑ भी अधिक दूर आरू अखनी भी गोपनीयता म॑ लिपटी गेलऽ छै ।

26 अगस्त क॑ हिमनदी केरऽ पतन स॑ शुरू होय वाला बाढ़ म॑ 1300 स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के जान गेलै आरू चारि गुना तलक के जान गेलै जे अखनी तलक लापता छै, जेकरा म॑ दर्जनों अमेरिकी भी शामिल छै । यू.एस.

ताजा आकलन स॑ पता चलै छै कि चीन केरऽ अपस्ट्रीम म॑ कोनो जलविद्युत स्टेशन नै छै, आरू ओकरऽ बुनियादी ढाँचा परियोजना बर्फ केरऽ हिमस्खलन म॑ कोनो भूमिका नै निभाबै सकै छेलै । लेकिन नदी के किनारे सिविल इंजीनियरिंग के काम के मुख्य योगदान चीन छै, ई लेली विशेषज्ञऽ के अनुमान छै कि घाटी म॑ ओकरऽ पुल, राजमार्ग आरू भवनऽ स॑ मलबा के बहाव के गति आरू संरचना म॑ बदलाव आबी गेलऽ होतै ।

दुनिया पर और पढ़ें

चीन आरू ओकरऽ पड़ोसी देश भारत न॑ जहाँ नेपाल प॑ प्रभाव लेली होड़ करै छै, वहीं नई दिल्ली म॑ बीजिंग केरऽ संदेहवादी के कहना छै कि हिमालय म॑ अपनऽ तरह के सबसें खराब आपदा तिब्बत केरऽ अन्य जगहऽ प॑ चीनी जलविद्युत योजना आरू नीचें के ओकरऽ प्रभाव के बारे म॑ चेतावनी के काम करना चाहियऽ । चीन एकर प्रतिकार क रहल अछि।

जखन आपदा अबैत अछि

उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी के सहायता स॑ मिललऽ प्रारंभिक रिपोर्ट म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि संभवतः भूस्खलन के शुरुआत १७,००० फीट स॑ भी अधिक ऊंचाई प॑, नेपाल केरऽ लंगटांग लिरुंग पर्वत केरऽ उत्तरी ढलान प॑ होय गेलऽ छै । यू.एस.

कीचड़ आरू बाढ़ केरऽ पानी केरऽ धार केरऽ पहलऽ तस्वीर चीन केरऽ ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह प॑ निगरानी कैमरा स॑ मिललऽ छेलै, जे कुछ ही सेकंड म॑ बह॑ गेलऽ छेलै । चीन के नेपाल के संग व्यापार के लेल ई सीमा पार मुख्य स्थल मार्ग छल.

बाढ़िक बाट मे रहनिहार आ काज करयवला लेल जे किछु कम पूर्व चेतावनी छल से बहुत देर सँ आबि गेल छल । प्लैनेट द्वारा उपलब्ध कराय देलऽ गेलऽ उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी म॑ तेजी स॑ चलै वाला बाढ़ केरऽ पानी केरऽ पीछू छोड़लऽ गेलऽ विनाश क॑ धरती प॑ एगो विशालकाय निशान के तरह देखालऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

...

जखन आपदा अबैत अछि त बीजिंग के पहिल प्रतिक्रिया अछि रोकथाम, नुकसान के मुदा जानकारी के सेहो.

बाढ़ि के घंटों के भीतर चीनी सोशल मीडिया ऐप पर गवाह द्वारा फिल्मायल गेल वीडियो के लगभग ओतबे जल्दी सेंसर भ गेल जतेक जल्दी अपलोड भ रहल छल. केवल स्वीकृत राज्य मीडिया फुटेज बचल छल, संगहि कोनो एहन वीडियो सेहो जे चीन के ग्रेट फायरवाल सं बाहर निकलल छल.

चीन सरकार क॑ ११ दिन लगलै कि विदेशी मीडिया क॑ ग्योरॉंग सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र स॑ रिपोर्ट करै के अनुमति मिल॑ सक॑ । बीजिंग केरऽ नियंत्रण केरऽ तीव्र जरूरत न॑ एगो जानकारीपूर्ण वैक्यूम पैदा करी देलकै जेकरा म॑ प्रतिकूल कथ्य खिललऽ छेलै ।

एकटा व्यापक उद्धृत बयान नेपालक पूर्व पर्यावरण मंत्री माधव प्रसाद चौलागैन के देल गेल अछि जे चीन नेपाल के बाढ़ि के बारे मे चेताबय मे असफल रहल कहलनि। एकटा भारतीय प्रसारक क॑ देलऽ गेलऽ ई टिप्पणी न॑ बीजिंग केरऽ जलवायु संबंधी आंकड़ा साझा करै म॑ कथित अनिच्छा के चलतें आलोचकऽ क॑ दिन भर पेट भरलकै ।

रायटर केरऽ रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, नेपाली अधिकारी न॑ आपदा स॑ तीन महीना पहल॑ चीनी समकक्षऽ स॑ पर्यावरण निगरानी केरऽ आंकड़ा मँगल॑ छेलै – जेकरा म॑ ग्लेशियर स॑ जुड़लऽ खतरा के बारे म॑ भी शामिल छेलै ।

सिंगापुर मैनेजमेंट यूनिवर्सिटी केरऽ कानून के प्रोफेसर हेनरी गाओ न॑ एक्स प॑ कहलकै कि बाकी दुनिया लेली ई व्यापक सबक ई छै कि चीन केरऽ सेंसरशिप आरू कवर-अप क॑ खाली चीनी लोगऽ क॑ प्रभावित करै वाला समस्या के रूप म॑ खारिज नै करलऽ जाय । अस्पष्टता राष्ट्रीय सीमा के भीतर नै रह॑ छै ।देर सबेर दोसरऽ जगहऽ के लोग भी एकरऽ लागत उठाबै सकै छै ।

गाओ नँ कहलकै, "अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समुदाय क चीन क अधिक पारदर्शी आरू जवाबदेह बनै लेली दबाव डालै के चाही। लेकिन जब तलक चीन मौलिक राजनीतिक सुधार नै करी क लोकतंत्र नै बनतै, तब तलक सार्थक जवाबदेही दुर्लभ रहतै।"

चीन नदी सब पर अपस्ट्रीम पर नियंत्रण रखैत अछि, आ जल स्तर के जानकारी के सामरिक रूप सं संवेदनशील मानल जा सकैत अछि. नेपाल के कहनाय छनि जे चीन के संग अपन सीमा पर सेंसर आओर कैमरा के इस्तेमाल सं अर्ली वार्निंग सिस्टम के फेर सं बनाओत, मुदा ओकर पड़ोसी देश पाछू हटय के पूरा मौका अछि.

एक्स पर भारतीय आरू नेपाली सोशल मीडिया यूजर्स नँ चीन के पारदर्शिता के कमी के कारण घातक बाढ़ के दोषी कहला के बाद काठमांडू मँ चीन के दूतावास नँ जवाबी गोलीबारी करतें कहलकै कि ई आरोप चीन के नेपाल के साथ सहयोग क बाधित करै लेली करलौ गेलौ छै ।

चीनी अधिकारी सब सूचना ब्लैकआउट के चिंता के जवाब दैत कहलनि जे, हुनका लग जे कोनो आंकड़ा अछि ओ पहिने सं साझा क रहल छथि। चीन केरऽ सरकारी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी न॑ कहलकै कि ग्लेशियर अक्सर हिलै छै आरू गिरै स॑ पहल॑ एकरऽ भविष्यवाणी करना मुश्किल छै ।

...

विशेषज्ञऽ के कहना छै कि हिमालय वैश्विक औसत स॑ दू गुना बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ हिमालय भूस्खलन आरू बाढ़ सहित पर्यावरणीय प्रलय के शिकार होय रहलऽ छै ।

पिछला सप्ताह नेपाल मे चीन के राजदूत झांग माओमिंग सरकारी स्वामित्व वाला अखबार राइजिंग नेपाल डेली मे चीनी प्रोफेसर के लिखल ओप-एड शेयर केने छलाह, जाहि मे एहि आपदा के दोष पश्चिम पर राखल गेल छल.

ओकरा मँ कहलौ गेलौ छै कि नेपाल आरू तिब्बती पठार मँ गर्मी स्थानीय उत्सर्जन के परिणाम नै छै-ई औद्योगिक ग्लोबल नॉर्थ केरौ संचित, सदियो पुरानौ कार्बन उत्सर्जन छै जे एक क्रायोस्फीयर प असर डालै छै, जेकरा प दोनों देश अपनौ जल सुरक्षा लेली निर्भर छै ।

नुकसान भ गेल अछि

चीन केरऽ नेता सब क॑ भागलऽ कथ्य केरऽ खतरा पता छै, महल म॑ तख्तापलट के बारे म॑ या कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी केरऽ शासन केरऽ अस्थिरता के बारे म॑ । एकरऽ सेंसरशिप केरऽ संबंध खाली कुछ हद तलक खराब नै देखै के इच्छा स॑ छेलै ।

बाहरी रूप स॑ बीजिंग क॑ ई बात के जानकारी होतै कि नेपाल आरू अन्य विकासशील देशऽ लेली एगो विश्वसनीय आर्थिक भागीदार के रूप म॑ अपनऽ भूमिका लेली ई आपदा के की मतलब छै । आंतरिक रूप स॑ एकरऽ प्रतिक्रिया तिब्बत क्षेत्र क॑ सुरक्षित रूप स॑ प्रबंधित करै के ओकरऽ क्षमता के बात करतै, जे नई दिल्ली के साथ तनाव के स्रोत छै, जे लगभग सात दशक स॑ उत्तरी भारत म॑ निर्वासित १४वां दलाई लामा के मेजबानी करी रहलऽ छै ।

हालांकि चीन केरऽ गोपनीयता केरऽ पसंद स॑ पूर्वी तिब्बत म॑ ओकरऽ हित क॑ सबसें जादा नुकसान पहुँचै सकै छै, जहां वू दुनिया केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ बांध एगो ऐसनऽ नदी प॑ बनाबै छै जेकरा स॑ नीचें करोड़ों लोगऽ के जान टिकैलऽ जाय छै ।

पिछला साल शुरू भेल आ 2030 के दशक में चलै वाला मेडोग जलविद्युत परियोजना भारत के ब्रह्मपुत्र आ बाद में बांग्लादेश के जमुना के महत्वपूर्ण मीठ जल स्रोत यारलुंग त्सांगपो पर चीनी नियंत्रण के ठोस बनाओत.

राजनीतिक रूप स॑ संवेदनशील तिब्बत केरऽ पूर्वी भाग म॑ लगभग एक दर्जन अलग-अलग आकार के बांध बनी चुकलऽ छै, जे भूवैज्ञानिक रूप स॑ नाजुक क्षेत्र छेकै जे पूर्व म॑ विनाशकारी भूकंप लेली जानलऽ जाय छै ।

नई दिल्ली केरऽ थिंक टैंक सेंटर फॉर पॉलिसी रिसर्च केरऽ रणनीतिक अध्ययन के प्रोफेसर ब्रह्म चेलानी न॑ नेपाल म॑ हिमनदीय पतन स॑ पहल॑ लिखलऽ गेलऽ एगो विश्लेषण म॑ कहलकै कि भूवैज्ञानिक खतरा कहानी केरऽ एगो हिस्सा ही छै ।

चेलानी नँ कहलकै, "ई सीमा पार के नदी प बांध के झरना बनैलकै, तनाव के दौर मँ जलविज्ञान के आंकड़ा रोकलकै, आरू डाउनस्ट्रीम राज्यौ के साथ जल साझा करै के कोनो भी संधि मँ प्रवेश करै के विरोध करलकै। पानी जबरन राज्य शिल्प के एगो आरू साधन बनी गेलौ छै।"

चीन सरकार न॑ अपनऽ "सदी केरऽ परियोजना" प॑ अतिरिक्त जांच लेली आमंत्रित करलकै, कैन्हेंकि वू सुपर डैम केरऽ पैमाना के बारे म॑ आरू विवरण नै देतै ।

शंघाई स्थित ऊर्जा विश्लेषक डेविड फिशमैन न॑ हाल ही म॑ सबस्टैक न्यूजलेटर म॑ कहलकै कि "हमरऽ नजर म॑ एगो गुप्त चीनी परियोजना के मतलब छै कि एकरा बारे म॑ विश्वसनीय जानकारी मिलना ककरो लेली मुश्किल छै, चीनी भाषा म॑ भी । पूर्वी तिब्बत केरऽ यारलुंग त्सांगपो नदी प॑ अब॑ निर्माणाधीन जलविद्युत मेगा परियोजना लेली भी यही हाल छै ।"

चीन के कहना छै कि 170 अरब डॉलर के ई बांध स॑ 60 गीगावाट बिजली पैदा होतै, जे मध्य चीन केरऽ थ्री गॉर्ज डैम स॑ तीन गुना अधिक छै – जे दुनिया केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ जलविद्युत सुविधा छै ।

फिशमैन न॑ कहलकै कि तभियो ई परियोजना केरऽ महत्वाकांक्षी पैमाना के बारे म॑ जेतना धूमधाम छै, ओकरा लेली जनता क॑ ई बात के बारे म॑ बहुत कम जानकारी छै कि ई केना सुविधा भी छै, निर्माण केरऽ मील के पत्थर, बिजली निर्यात गंतव्य, आसपास के पर्यावरण प॑ पड़ै वाला प्रभाव, या मानव आबादी प॑ अपेक्षित प्रभाव जैसनऽ विवरण के बात क॑ कभियो नै ।

नेपाल केरऽ आपदा के बाद स॑ एक्स प॑ भारतीय सोशल मीडिया यूजर आरू अन्य कमेंटेटर न॑ चीन केरऽ मेगा डैम क॑ एगो “टाइम बम” बतैलकै जेकरा स॑ भारत प॑ खतरा पैदा होय सकै छै ।

चीन एहि बात सं असहमत भ’ सकैत अछि मुदा जानकारी साझा करबा मे ओकर अनिच्छा के मतलब अछि जे ओ दोसर के कथ्य पर नियंत्रण राखय दैत अछि.

प्रतिस्पर्धी हिमालय पर आपसी विश्वास कम अछि, आ ई कम होमय बला अछि.

full_article:
Buddhist monks prepare for a requiem ceremony for the victims of the devastating flash floods that struck Nepal on August 26. (Photo: AP)

The national flags were flown at half-mast at government offices nationwide and Nepali diplomatic missions abroad.

People performed memorial rituals and offered tributes to the deceased. As search and rescue operations remain underway, Nepal did not hold large-scale memorial ceremonies on the national day of mourning. President Ram Chandra Paudel was touring flood-hit areas to survey damage caused by the disaster.

Oil lamps are lit during a requiem ceremony for the victims. (Photo: AP)

The Nepalese Army said that the rescue efforts continue at "the same tempo" to make sure "that no one is still stranded" and are focusing on ground areas, from the air, and inside tunnel systems.

As of Monday morning, the flash flood disaster in the border region between Nepal and China killed 1,385 people and more than 5,500 others still missing.

title: As Nepal identifies those killed in the floods, questions grow over China's reporting - NPR
description: As Nepal identifies those killed in the floods, questions grow over China's reporting  NPR
publisher.title: NPR
full_article:
Relatives of recent flash flood victims hold banners urging authorities to step up efforts to find their missing loved ones during a demonstration in Kathmandu, Nepal, on Monday. Dar Yasin/AP hide caption toggle caption Dar Yasin/AP

BEIJING — Shortly after the deadly flash floods hit the border of Nepal and China on Aug. 26, Nepalese authorities released a list of names, ages and nationalities of hundreds of missing foreigners. In contrast, Chinese authorities took five days to disclose that the 261 foreigners missing in Tibet come from 23 countries.

State of the World from NPR Rescuing those still trapped by flash floods in Nepal and Tibet

Twelve days on, very little is known about the victims in Tibet as Chinese authorities have restricted reporting on the floods.

To date, Nepal has reported over 1,300 dead and nearly 5,000 missing, while China is reporting over 40 dead and more than 500 missing.

"Xinhua (state-run news agency) and (state broadcaster) CCTV have total information dominance," said David Bandurski in Taipei with the China Media Project, which monitors news censorship in China.

These outlets are expected to "guide public opinion," he said.

While China has always censored information, controls have tightened steadily over the last decade, he said to levels that are "unprecedented."

Sponsor Message

No independent access

Rights groups that have been closely following the disaster relief say the lack of independent access to the area of the flooding in Gyirong County in Tibet is striking.

"This is in contrast to the Nepal side of the border where there was immediate access given for journalists, for other observers, for international humanitarian relief organizations," said Ryan Fioresi of the DC-based International Campaign for Tibet.

To report on the rescue efforts in Nepal, NPR was able to check in with international aid agencies on the ground and speak with a rescue pilot . Nepal's police, disaster management authority and the tourism board have also been providing regular updates on their social media feeds.

Whereas in China, the government restricts foreign journalists from entering the politically sensitive region.

It took more than a week of repeated requests from multiple international media outlets before the Chinese government allowed foreign journalists in Tibet.

People take part in a candlelight vigil for victims of the floods in Nepal and Tibet, at Durbar Square in Kathmandu, Nepal, Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. Dar Yasin/AP hide caption toggle caption Dar Yasin/AP

However, it was limited to a small number of foreign outlets in a carefully arranged visit. NPR was not granted access.

The International Campaign for Tibet claims at least 300 homes were destroyed in Gyirong County, and Fioresi said the casualty count could be "much higher" than the dozens reported by Chinese officials so far.

Sponsor Message

He also said Tibetans in the worst affected areas were relocated to "tightly controlled holding areas."

"Their communications with the outside world have been extremely limited and curtailed," Fioresi said, adding that it hampers local rescue efforts.

Asia Nepal's hesitance to accept foreign help for flood relief comes under scrutiny

China's foreign ministry has not responded to NPR's request for comment.

However, in an earlier briefing with reporters in Beijing, foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun denied China was understating the number of missing and dead, saying China has been "open, transparent and timely in information release."

"Smear and disinformation is most unwelcome at a time of disaster response," Guo said.

How different Chinese media are covering the tragedy

China's commercial media, which were still subject to censorship but had more leeway, would have sent journalists to a disaster site quickly in the past, according to Rose Luqiu, an associate professor of journalism at Hong Kong Baptist University who studies Chinese propaganda and censorship.

She said she saw the Beijing News and Southern Weekly had tried to do some of their own reporting.

China Fire and Rescue personnel arrive at Trishuli camp after inspecting the tunnel site in Rasuwa, in the aftermath of flash floods in Nepal's Nuwakot district on August 31, 2026. Rescuers struggled on August 31 through mud and debris for a sixth day, as the number of missing people soared to nearly 5,000 since tsunami-like glacial floods roared down from the China-Nepal border, creating an "unimaginable" disaster. ARUN SANKAR/AFP hide caption toggle caption ARUN SANKAR/AFP

"For example they tried to interview tourists. Not victims or those directly impacted in the local villages but they're trying to … provide some more information," she said.

In the 2008 Sichuan earthquake, various Chinese media outlets sent hundreds of journalists to the scene "in direct violation of an explicit ban from the central propaganda department of the Communist Party," Bandurski said.

This time, he said, the Southern Metropolis Daily , known for its journalistic investigations, ran only one front page cover on the floods in the days after the disaster, and it was an article reprinted from the official Xinhua news agency.

"They didn't do additional reporting," Bandurski said, adding that it was unusual for the paper.

Bandurski said his team saw the same pattern in other commercial Chinese media outlets.

"Xi Jinping has reined in the [commercial] press, such as it was developing in the 2000s," he said. "We see a total control of the narrative and basic news and information."

Sponsor Message

Foreign ministry spokesperson Guo has denied China deletes videos and first-hand accounts online.

A Buddhist monk offers prayers for the departed soul of the victims of flash flood on the bank of Trishuli river in Devighat, Nuwakot district, Nepal, Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. Niranjan Shrestha/AP hide caption toggle caption Niranjan Shrestha/AP

But many of the videos that were circulating widely after the floods were being actively deleted, according to Bandurski.

Recently the Chinese police penalized 10 people for spreading what they called misinformation about the floods.

Chinese state media, such as Xinhua, CCTV and Tibet Daily, have sent journalists with rescue teams, sometimes hiking overnight with them at high altitudes, sleeping openly under the rain, to reach the worst affected area at the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing.

The focus of their coverage is on the rescue teams, logistics of the operations and how government leaders are reacting quickly to the disaster, according Luqiu.

World Families of pilgrims likely caught in floods are desperate for news from Nepal

She said there are state media reports on people affected by the floods, but compared with the reports on the rescue operations, "the situation about the victims and the village members is relatively very small."
translated:
नेपाल के काठमांडू मे सोमदिन प्रदर्शन के दौरान हाल के आकस्मिक बाढ़ पीड़ित के परिजन के हाथ मे बैनर लागल अछि जाहि मे अधिकारि सं अपन लापता प्रियजन के खोजय के प्रयास तेज करय के आग्रह कएल गेल अछि. दार यासिन/एपी कैप्शन छिपाएँ कैप्शन टॉगल दार यासीन/एपी

बीजिंग : 26 अगस्त क॑ नेपाल आरू चीन केरऽ सीमा प॑ घातक आकस्मिक बाढ़ के कुछ देर बाद नेपाली अधिकारियऽ न॑ सैकड़ों लापता विदेशी के नाम, उम्र आरू राष्ट्रीयता के सूची जारी करलकै । एकरऽ विपरीत चीनी अधिकारियऽ क॑ ई खुलासा करै म॑ पाँच दिन लगलै कि तिब्बत म॑ लापता २६१ विदेशी २३ देशऽ स॑ छै ।

एनपीआर सँ विश्व अवस्था नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे एखनहु आकस्मिक बाढ़ि मे फँसल लोकक उद्धार

बारह दिन बाद तिब्बत मे पीड़ित के बारे मे बहुत कम जानकारी अछि किएक त चीनी अधिकारी बाढ़ि के रिपोर्टिंग पर रोक लगा देने छथिन्ह.

आइ धरि नेपाल मे १३०० सँ बेसी मृतक आ लगभग ५ हजार लापता भेल अछि, जखन कि चीन मे ४० सँ बेसी मृतक आ ५०० सँ बेसी लापता होयबाक सूचना भेटि रहल अछि ।

चीन मँ समाचार सेंसरशिप के निगरानी करै वाला चाइना मीडिया प्रोजेक्ट के साथ ताइपे मँ डेविड बांदुर्स्की नँ कहलकै कि सिन्हुआ (सरकारी समाचार एजेंसी) आरू (राज्य प्रसारक) सीसीटीवी मँ कुल सूचना के वर्चस्व छै ।

ओ कहला जे एहि आउटलेट स “जनमत कए मार्गदर्शन” करबाक उम्मीद अछि।

चीन हमेशा स॑ ही जानकारी क॑ सेंसर करी रहलऽ छै, लेकिन पिछला एक दशक म॑ नियंत्रण लगातार कड़ा होय गेलऽ छै, ई बात क॑ हुनी कहलकै कि ई स्तर प॑ अभूतपूर्व छै ।

प्रायोजक संदेश

कोनो स्वतंत्र पहुँच नहि

आपदा राहत केरऽ बारीकी स॑ पालन करी रहलऽ अधिकार समूहऽ के कहना छै कि तिब्बत केरऽ ग्यिरॉंग काउंटी म॑ बाढ़ केरऽ इलाका म॑ स्वतंत्र पहुँच के कमी हड़ताली छै ।

डीसी स्थित इंटरनेशनल कैंपेन फॉर तिब्बत के रयान फिओरेसी कहलनि जे, ई सीमा के नेपाल पक्ष के विपरीत अछि जतय पत्रकार के लेल, अन्य पर्यवेक्षक के लेल, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानवीय राहत संगठन के तत्काल पहुंच देल गेल छल।

नेपाल मे बचाव प्रयास के रिपोर्ट करय लेल एनपीआर जमीन पर अंतरराष्ट्रीय सहायता एजेंसी सं जांच करय मे सफल रहल आओर एकटा बचाव पायलट सं बात करय मे सफल रहल . नेपाल के पुलिस, आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण आ पर्यटन बोर्ड सेहो अपन सोशल मीडिया फीड पर नियमित अपडेट दैत आबि रहल अछि।

जखन कि चीन मे सरकार विदेशी पत्रकार कए राजनीतिक रूप स संवेदनशील क्षेत्र मे प्रवेश करबा पर रोक लगा दैत अछि।

चीन सरकार न॑ विदेशी पत्रकारऽ क॑ तिब्बत म॑ जाय के अनुमति दै म॑ एक सप्ताह स॑ भी अधिक समय लगलै कि कईएक अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मीडिया केरऽ बार-बार आग्रह करलऽ गेलै ।

नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे बाढ़ि मे पीड़ित लोकनिक लेल मोमबत्ती जराओल जागरण मे लोक भाग लैत छथि, नेपालक काठमांडू के दरबार चौक पर, शनि दिन, 5 सितम्बर 2026. दार यासिन/एपी hide caption toggle caption दार यासिन/ए.पी

मुदा, सावधानीपूर्वक व्यवस्था कयल गेल यात्रा मे ई थोड़-बहुत विदेशी आउटलेट धरि सीमित छल. एनपीआर कए पहुंच नहि देल गेल।

तिब्बत केरऽ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अभियान के दावा छै कि ग्योरोंग काउंटी म॑ कम स॑ कम ३०० घर तबाह होय गेलऽ छै, आरू फिओरेसी न॑ कहलकै कि चीनी अधिकारियऽ द्वारा अब तलक के दर्जनों घरऽ स॑ जानमाल के नुकसान के गिनती “बहुत अधिक” होय सकै छै ।

प्रायोजक संदेश

हुनी ई भी कहलकै कि सबसें जादा प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ के तिब्बती लोगऽ क॑ “कड़ा नियंत्रण वाला होल्डिंग क्षेत्र” म॑ स्थानांतरित करी देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

फिओरेसी नँ कहलकै कि बाहरी दुनिया के साथ हुनकौ संवाद अत्यंत सीमित आरू कटौती करलौ गेलौ छै आरू कहलकै कि ई स्थानीय बचाव प्रयास मँ बाधा पहुँचै छै ।

बाढ़ि राहत लेल विदेशी सहायता स्वीकार करबा मे एशिया नेपालक संकोच पर नजरि आबि रहल अछि

चीन के विदेश मंत्रालय एनपीआर के कोनो टिप्पणी के आग्रह के कोनो जवाब नै देलक अछि।

लेकिन बीजिंग म॑ पत्रकारऽ के साथ पहलऽ ब्रिफिंग म॑ विदेश मंत्रालय केरऽ प्रवक्ता गुओ जियाकुन न॑ चीन स॑ लापता आरू मृतकऽ के संख्या क॑ कम बताबै स॑ इनकार करतें हुअ॑ कहलकै कि चीन न॑ सूचना जारी करै म॑ खुला, पारदर्शी आरू समय पर रहलऽ छै ।

गुओ कहलनि जे, आपदा के प्रतिक्रिया के समय मे धब्बा आ गलत सूचना सबस बेसी अवांछनीय अछि।

कोना अलग-अलग चीनी मीडिया एहि त्रासदी कए कवर क रहल अछि

चीनी प्रचार आ सेंसरशिप के अध्ययन करय वाला हांगकांग बैपटिस्ट विश्वविद्यालय के पत्रकारिता के एसोसिएट प्रोफेसर रोज लुकिउ के अनुसार चीन के वाणिज्यिक मीडिया जे एखनो सेंसरशिप के अधीन छल मुदा ओकरा बेसी छूट छल, पहिने पत्रकार के जल्दी सं आपदा स्थल पर भेज दैत.

ओ कहली जे ओ देखलनि जे बीजिंग न्यूज आ साउथर्न वीकली अपन किछु रिपोर्टिंग करबाक कोशिश केलक अछि।

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में 31 अगस्त 2026 के झटका बाढ़ के बाद रसुवा में सुरंग स्थल के निरीक्षण के बाद चीन फायर एंड रेस्क्यू के जवान त्रिशुली शिविर पहुंचल अछि चीन-नेपाल सीमा स बाढ़ि गर्जैत नीचाँ गर्जैत एकटा "अकल्पनीय" आपदा उत्पन्न केलक । अरुण संकर/एएफपी कैप्शन छिपाओ टॉगल कैप्शन अरुण संकर/एएफपी

"उदाहरण के लेल ओ सब पर्यटक के साक्षात्कार लेबाक कोशिश केलनि।" पीड़ित या स्थानीय गाम मे सीधा प्रभावित लोक नहि मुदा ओ कोशिश क रहल छथि जे ... किछ आओर जानकारी देल जाए।'

बांडर्स्की नँ कहलकै कि २००८ मँ सिचुआन भूकंप मँ चीनी विभिन्न मीडिया नँ सैकड़ों पत्रकार क मौका प भेजलकै, जेकरा मँ “कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी केरौ केंद्रीय प्रचार विभाग केरौ स्पष्ट प्रतिबंध के सीधा उल्लंघन” करलौ गेलौ छेलै ।

हुनी कहलकै कि ई बार पत्रकारिता के जांच लेली जानलऽ जाय वाला दक्षिणी महानगर दैनिक न॑ आपदा के बाद के दिनऽ म॑ बाढ़ प॑ खाली एगो फ्रंट पेज के कवर चलाबै छेलै, आरू ई एगो लेख छेलै जेकरा आधिकारिक सिन्हुआ न्यूज एजेंसी स॑ दोबारा छपलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

बांडुरस्की कहलनि जे, ओ सब अतिरिक्त रिपोर्टिंग नहि केलनि आ पेपर लेल ई असामान्य अछि।

बांदुर्स्की न॑ कहलकै कि हुनकऽ टीम क॑ चीनी केरऽ अन्य वाणिज्यिक मीडिया म॑ भी यही पैटर्न देखलऽ गेलै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, शी जिनपिंग [व्यावसायिक] प्रेस पर लगाम लगेने छथि, जेना कि 2000 के दशक मे एकर विकास भ रहल छल। "हमरा सब क॑ कथ्य आरू बुनियादी समाचार आरू जानकारी प॑ पूर्ण नियंत्रण देखै ल॑ मिलै छै ।"

प्रायोजक संदेश

विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता गुओ चीन के वीडियो आओर फर्स्ट हैंड अकाउंट ऑनलाइन डिलीट करय सं इनकार क देलखिन्ह.

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला के देवीघाट के त्रिशुली नदी के किनारे पर 5 सितम्बर 2026 शनिवार के झटका बाढ़ के शिकार के दिवंगत आत्मा के लेल प्रार्थना करैत एकटा बौद्ध भिक्षु निरंजन श्रेष्ठ/एपी hide caption toggle caption निरंजन श्रेष्ठ/एपी

लेकिन बाढ़ के बाद जे वीडियो व्यापक रूप स॑ घूमी रहलऽ छेलै, ओकरा म॑ स॑ बहुत सारा वीडियो क॑ सक्रिय रूप स॑ डिलीट करी देलऽ जाय रहलऽ छेलै, बांदुर्स्की के अनुसार ।

हालहि मे चीनी पुलिस बाढ़ि के बारे मे जेकरा ओ गलत जानकारी कहैत छल, ओकरा फैलााबय वाला 10 लोक के दंडित केलक अछि.

चीनी सरकारी मीडिया, जेना कि सिन्हुआ, सीसीटीवी आरू तिब्बत डेली न॑ पत्रकारऽ क॑ बचाव टीम के साथ भेजलकै, जेकरा म॑ कखनी-कखनी ओकरा साथ रात भर ऊंचऽ ऊंचाई प॑ पैदल यात्रा करी क॑, बारिश के नीचे खुल क॑ सुतलऽ छै, ताकि ग्यरोंग-रासुवा सीमा क्रासिंग प॑ सबसें बेसी प्रभावित इलाका म॑ पहुँचलऽ जाय सक॑ ।

लुकिउ के अनुसार, हुनकऽ कवरेज के फोकस बचाव टीम, ऑपरेशन केरऽ रसद आरू आपदा प॑ सरकारी नेता सिनी के प्रतिक्रिया केना जल्दी स॑ होय रहलऽ छै, ई प॑ छै ।

विश्व बाढ़ि मे फँसल संभवतः तीर्थयात्रीक परिवार नेपाल सँ खबरि लेल बेताब अछि

हुनी कहलकै कि बाढ़ स॑ प्रभावित लोगऽ के बारे म॑ सरकारी मीडिया म॑ रिपोर्ट छै, लेकिन बचाव अभियान के रिपोर्ट के तुलना म॑ “पीड़ित आरू गाँव के सदस्यऽ के बारे म॑ स्थिति अपेक्षाकृत बहुत कम छै ।

title: The Tibet-Nepal flood is a warning against defying nature - Stagecraft and Statecraft
description: The Tibet-Nepal flood is a warning against defying nature  Stagecraft and Statecraft
publisher.title: Stagecraft and Statecraft
full_article:
The Nepal-Tibet catastrophe unfolded just as two international scientific studies had anticipated by modelling how flood surges behave as they emerge from engineered corridors in the Tibetan border region into downstream Nepal.

Debris from a bridge damaged by flash flooding lies along the banks of the swollen Trishuli River at 1 Number Pul, in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. AP Photo.

By Brahma Chellaney, The Hill

Humanity is altering natural ecosystems more rapidly than it is developing an adequate scientific understanding of the consequences. Those alterations are contributing to climate change, which in turn is amplifying the damage to ecosystems. The Nepal-Tibet flood disaster is a stark reminder that humanity must stop trying to bend nature to its will.

The catastrophe that began high in the mighty Himalayas on the Tibet-Nepal border is a warning from the world’s youngest, tallest and most volatile mountain range about the dangerous illusion that humans can engineer nature into submission.

An immense ice-and-rock avalanche sheared off a glacier situated directly along the crest of the international boundary on the Nepalese side, plunged into the China-controlled Tibetan upper basin, and unleashed a devastating torrent that ripped through transboundary rivers, wrecking upstream Chinese infrastructure and leaving a vast trail of death and destruction downstream in Nepal.

The disaster exemplified how human interventions can magnify nature’s fury. Nepal bore no responsibility for the catastrophic flash floods, yet it faced their main brunt. Extensive infrastructure-centered alterations to the upstream river corridor and mountain landscape in the Tibetan border region compounded the downstream effects through physical, structural and operational vulnerabilities.

The tragedy’s central lesson is best summed up by the 1970s American television advertising slogan that became a pop-culture catchphrase: “It’s not nice to fool Mother Nature.”

In the name of development, countries have long sought to redirect river flows, flatten mountains, tame weather and conquer landscapes. Such engineering has undeniably brought energy, water and prosperity. But when it disregards the fundamental logic of natural systems, manageable risks potentially turn into calamitous ones.

The Tibet-Nepal disaster offers the latest illustration of why respecting nature has become an imperative for humanity’s future.

Yet much of the analysis of this disaster in U.S. and international media has focused on climate change while obscuring how human alteration of ecosystems is itself increasing natural hazards and accelerating global warming. Climate change should not become a catch-all explanation that deflects attention from the broader ecological and environmental damage caused by human activity. Climate change is one consequence of these wider human impacts.

The unstable Himalayas are a living geological laboratory. Large-scale construction and river engineering there can significantly compound risk.

Pounded by the slow-motion collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates, the Himalayas remain among the most seismically active and structurally fragile regions on Earth. Their rocks continue to fracture and rise; glaciers expand and retreat; and monsoon rains and freeze-thaw cycles constantly weaken steep valley walls. In such an environment, landslides, cryospheric collapses and flash floods are anything but rare.

The latest catastrophe underscores that inherent instability. But what followed the initial act of nature was shaped as much by human construction as by natural processes.

Natural floodplains, gravel bars and meandering channels act as hydraulic shock absorbers, dissipating energy by allowing water to spread laterally. When they are replaced with concrete embankments, retaining walls, highways, diversion structures and narrowed channels, the river system loses its natural flood buffer. Water is forced into tighter corridors from Tibet, accelerating its speed and increasing its destructive power in Nepal, as a 2022 scientific study had forewarned.

That is exactly how the flood tragedy appears to have unfolded, with extensive embankments, border facilities, highways, intake works and riverbank engineering creating artificial bottlenecks in the upper Tibetan valley. Instead of allowing the floodwaters and debris to disperse naturally, these structures funneled the liquid-rock-mud mass through a narrow gorge, dramatically increasing its velocity before it surged downstream into Nepal’s river basins.

This resulted in devastating consequences. Loose sediment and debris from upstream construction sites were swept into the deluge, creating a dense, hyper-concentrated slurry that smashed bridges, roads, buildings and hydropower infrastructure with enormous kinetic force. Temporary debris dams formed behind bridges and culverts before bursting, releasing secondary flood pulses that were even more destructive than the original surge, as another peer-reviewed study had foreseen.

The tragedy fits into a much broader global pattern. Modern states increasingly pursue projects that seek to reshape natural systems.

China has become the world’s most ambitious practitioner of this approach — from its environmentally damaging Three Gorges Dam and gigantic South-to-North Water Diversion Project to massive weather-modification programs and the colossal super-dam now rising on Tibet’s Yarlung Tsangpo, the world’s highest-altitude major river. Such projects reflect a seductive belief that nature can be bent to the Chinese will.

Complex ecosystems, however, rarely behave like human-made machines. Natural systems function through intricate networks of feedback and balance. Every significant human intervention can alter interconnected natural processes whose cumulative effects may emerge years later or even in places far removed from where the original construction occurred.

The Tibet-Nepal disaster is a strong expression of a universal truth: disrupting one component of a tightly connected natural system creates cascading consequences throughout the whole.

Humanity has entered an age in which its engineering capacity has become extraordinary, but so too has its ability to magnify natural hazards. It is thus imperative for humanity to understand its safe operating space.

Respecting Mother Nature does not mean abandoning development or rejecting engineering. It means recognizing that human ingenuity must work with natural processes rather than against them.

The sustainable path is stewardship, not mastery, of nature. It includes protecting floodplains instead of endlessly constricting rivers, preserving biodiversity instead of simplifying ecosystems, and designing infrastructure that accommodates natural flows rather than reengineering them.

We can keep trying to bend nature to human ambition and greed, or learn to live within nature’s design. The Himalayas have delivered their verdict with clarity.

Brahma Chellaney is the author of nine books, including the award-winning “ Water: Asia’s New Battleground. “

नेपाल-तिब्बत प्रलय ठीक ओहिना खुलल जेना दूटा अंतर्राष्ट्रीय वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन मे बाढ़िक लहर तिब्बती सीमा क्षेत्र मे इंजीनियरिंग गलियारा स डाउनस्ट्रीम नेपाल मे निकलैत काल केहन व्यवहार करैत अछि ओकर मॉडलिंग कए अनुमान लगाउल गेल छल ।

ब्रह्म चेलानी द्वारा, द हिल

मानवता प्राकृतिक पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र म॑ बदलाव करी रहलऽ छै, जेतना तेजी स॑ एकरऽ परिणाम के बारे म॑ पर्याप्त वैज्ञानिक समझ विकसित करी रहलऽ छै । ओ परिवर्तन जलवायु परिवर्तन मे योगदान द रहल छै, जे बदला मे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र कें नुकसान कें बढ़ा रहल छै. नेपाल-तिब्बत बाढ़िक आपदा एकटा घोर स्मरण कराबैत अछि जे मानवता केँ प्रकृति केँ अपन मर्जी सँ मोड़बाक प्रयास छोड़बाक चाही।

तिब्बत-नेपाल सीमा पर पराक्रमी हिमालय में ऊँच पर शुरू भेल प्रलय दुनिया के सब सं कम उम्र के, ऊँच आ अस्थिर पर्वत श्रृंखला के तरफ सं एहि खतरनाक भ्रम के चेतावनी अछि जे मनुक्ख प्रकृति के अधीनता में इंजीनियरिंग क सकैत अछि.

एकटा अपार बर्फ-चट्टानक हिमस्खलन नेपाली दिसक सीधा अंतरराष्ट्रीय सीमाक शिखाक कात में अवस्थित एकटा ग्लेशियर कें कतरल, चीन द्वारा नियंत्रित तिब्बती ऊपरी बेसिन में डूबि गेल आ एकटा विनाशकारी धार छोड़लक जे सीमा पारक नदी सब कें फाड़ि क' ऊपरक चीनी बुनियादी ढाँचा कें ध्वस्त क देलक आ नेपाल में नीचां में मृत्यु आ विनाशक विशाल निशान छोड़ि देलक.

ई आपदा उदाहरण देलकै कि कोना मानवीय हस्तक्षेप प्रकृति केरऽ आक्रोश क॑ बढ़ाबै सकै छै । नेपाल केरऽ ई विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ केरऽ कोय जिम्मेदारी नै छेलै, तभियो ओकरा ओकरऽ मुख्य बोझ के सामना करना पड़लै । तिब्बती सीमा क्षेत्र मँ अपस्ट्रीम नदी गलियारा आरू पहाड़ी परिदृश्य मँ व्यापक बुनियादी ढाँचा केंद्रित परिवर्तन नँ भौतिक, संरचनात्मक आरू परिचालन कमजोरी के माध्यम स॑ डाउनस्ट्रीम प्रभाव क॑ और बढ़ा देलकै ।

त्रासदी केरऽ केंद्रीय पाठ क॑ सबसें अच्छा संक्षेप म॑ 1970 के दशक केरऽ अमेरिकी टेलीविजन विज्ञापन नारा स॑ कहलऽ जाय छै जे पॉप-संस्कृति केरऽ कैचफ्रेज बनी गेलै: “प्रकृति माता क॑ बेवकूफ बनाना अच्छा नै छै ।”

विकास के नाम पर देश बहुत दिन स नदी के बहाव के पुनर्निर्देशित करय, पहाड़ के समतल करय, मौसम के वश में करय आ परिदृश्य के जीतय के कोशिश करैत रहल अछि. एहन इंजीनियरिंग निर्विवाद रूप स ऊर्जा, जल आ समृद्धि कए अनलक अछि। लेकिन जब॑ ई प्राकृतिक प्रणाली केरऽ मौलिक तर्क के अवहेलना करै छै त॑ प्रबंधनीय जोखिम संभावित रूप स॑ आपदाजनक म॑ बदली जाय छै ।

तिब्बत-नेपाल आपदा एहि बातक नवीनतम उदाहरण दैत अछि जे प्रकृतिक सम्मान मानवताक भविष्यक लेल किएक अनिवार्य बनि गेल अछि |

तइयो अमेरिकी आरू अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मीडिया म॑ ई आपदा केरऽ बहुत सारा विश्लेषण जलवायु परिवर्तन प॑ केंद्रित छै जबकि ई अस्पष्ट करलऽ गेलऽ छै कि पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र म॑ मानवीय परिवर्तन खुद प्राकृतिक खतरा क॑ बढ़ाबै आरू ग्लोबल वार्मिंग म॑ तेजी लानी रहलऽ छै । जलवायु परिवर्तन कें एकटा एहन कैच-ऑल व्याख्या नहि बनबाक चाही जे मानव गतिविधि सं होएय वाला व्यापक पारिस्थितिकी आ पर्यावरणीय क्षति सं ध्यान भटकाबय. जलवायु परिवर्तन एहि व्यापक मानवीय प्रभावक एकटा परिणाम अछि ।

अस्थिर हिमालय एकटा जीवित भूवैज्ञानिक प्रयोगशाला अछि । ओतय पैघ पैमाना पर निर्माण आ नदी इंजीनियरिंग जोखिम कें काफी बढ़ा सकय छै.

भारतीय आरू यूरेशियन विवर्तनिक प्लेट केरऽ धीमी गति के टक्कर स॑ टकराबै वाला हिमालय पृथ्वी केरऽ सबसें भूकंपीय रूप स॑ सक्रिय आरू संरचनात्मक रूप स॑ नाजुक क्षेत्रऽ म॑ शामिल छै । हुनका लोकनिक चट्टान टूटैत रहैत छनि आ उठैत रहैत छनि; ग्लेशियरक विस्तार आ पाछू हटि जाइत अछि; आरू मानसून केरऽ बारिश आरू फ्रीज-थॉ चक्र लगातार खड़ा घाटी केरऽ देवाल क॑ कमजोर करी दै छै । एहन वातावरण मे भूस्खलन, क्रायोस्फीयर ढहब आ फ्लैश फ्लड किछुओ नहि अछि मुदा दुर्लभ अछि ।

नवीनतम प्रलय ओहि अंतर्निहित अस्थिरता केँ रेखांकित करैत अछि । मुदा प्रकृतिक प्रारंभिक क्रियाक बाद जे किछु भेलैक ओकर आकार ओतबे मानवीय निर्माणसँ भेलैक जतेक प्राकृतिक प्रक्रियासँ ।

प्राकृतिक बाढ़ कें मैदान, गिट्टी कें सलाख आ घुमावदार चैनल हाइड्रोलिक सदमे अवशोषक कें रूप मे काज करएयत छै, जे पानी कें पार्श्विक रूप सं फैलएय कें अनुमति द क ऊर्जा कें विसर्जित करएयत छै. जखन एकरऽ जगह प॑ कंक्रीट केरऽ तटबंध, रिटेनिंग वॉल, हाईवे, डायवर्सन संरचना आरू संकुचित चैनल लगाय देलऽ जाय छै त॑ नदी प्रणाली केरऽ प्राकृतिक बाढ़ बफर खतम होय जाय छै । तिब्बत स॑ पानी क॑ कड़ा गलियारा म॑ मजबूर करलऽ जाय छै, जेकरा स॑ एकरऽ गति तेज होय जाय छै आरू नेपाल म॑ एकरऽ विनाशकारी शक्ति बढ़ी जाय छै, जैसनऽ कि २०२२ केरऽ वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन म॑ पूर्व चेतावनी देलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

बाढ़ केरऽ त्रासदी ठीक वैसनऽ ही खुललऽ नजर आबी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ व्यापक तटबंध, सीमा सुविधा, राजमार्ग, इंटेक वर्क आरू नदी केरऽ किनारे इंजीनियरिंग के वजह स॑ ऊपरी तिब्बती घाटी म॑ कृत्रिम अड़चन पैदा होय गेलऽ छै । बाढ़ के पानी आरू मलबा क॑ प्राकृतिक रूप स॑ फैलै के बजाय ई संरचना सब तरल-चट्टान-कीचड़ केरऽ द्रव्यमान क॑ एक संकीर्ण गॉर्ज के माध्यम स॑ फनल करी क॑ नीचें नेपाल केरऽ नदी बेसिन म॑ उछली स॑ पहल॑ एकरऽ वेग म॑ नाटकीय रूप स॑ वृद्धि करी देलकै ।

एकर परिणाम विनाशकारी भेल। अपस्ट्रीम निर्माण स्थलऽ स॑ निकललऽ ढीला तलछट आरू मलबा क॑ बाढ़ म॑ बहाय देलऽ गेलै, जेकरा स॑ एक घना, अति-केंद्रित स्लरी पैदा होय गेलै जे पुल, सड़क, भवन आरू जलविद्युत बुनियादी ढाँचा क॑ भारी गतिज बल स॑ तोड़ी देलकै । पुल आरू कलवर्ट के पीछू अस्थायी मलबा बांध फटै स॑ पहल॑ बनलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ गौण बाढ़ के दाल निकलै छेलै जे मूल उछाल स॑ भी अधिक विनाशकारी छेलै, जैसनऽ कि एगो आरू साथी-समीक्षित अध्ययन म॑ पूर्वानुमान छेलै ।

त्रासदी एकटा बहुत व्यापक वैश्विक पैटर्न मे फिट बैसैत अछि। आधुनिक राज्य तेजी सं एहन परियोजनाक कें पीछा करय छै जे प्राकृतिक प्रणाली कें नव रूप देनाय कें कोशिश करय छै.

चीन ई दृष्टिकोण केरऽ दुनिया केरऽ सबसें महत्वाकांक्षी अभ्यासकर्ता बनी गेलऽ छै — अपनऽ पर्यावरण के नुकसान पहुँचै वाला थ्री गॉर्ज डैम आरू विशालकाय दक्षिण-टू-उत्तर जल डायवर्सन परियोजना स॑ ल॑ क॑ मौसम-संशोधन केरऽ भारी कार्यक्रम आरू दुनिया केरऽ सबस॑ अधिक ऊंचाई वाला प्रमुख नदी तिब्बत केरऽ यारलुंग त्सांगपो प॑ अब॑ उठलऽ विशाल सुपर-डैम तक । एहन परियोजना एकटा मोहक विश्वास कए दर्शाबैत अछि जे प्रकृति कए चीनी इच्छा क प्रति झुकाउल जा सकैत अछि ।

जटिल पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र, तथापि, मानव निर्मित मशीन जकाँ बहुत कम व्यवहार करैत अछि । प्राकृतिक प्रणाली प्रतिक्रिया आ संतुलन कें जटिल जाल कें माध्यम सं काज करएयत छै. मानव केरऽ हर महत्वपूर्ण हस्तक्षेप परस्पर जुड़लऽ प्राकृतिक प्रक्रिया म॑ बदलाव लानी सकै छै जेकरऽ संचयी प्रभाव सालऽ बाद या यहाँ तलक कि मूल निर्माण घटित होय वाला जगहऽ स॑ बहुत दूर भी उभर॑ सकै छै ।

तिब्बत-नेपाल आपदा एकटा सार्वभौमिक सत्यक सशक्त अभिव्यक्ति अछि : कस क' जुड़ल प्राकृतिक व्यवस्थाक एकटा घटक केँ बाधित करला सँ समग्रता मे झरना सन परिणाम उत्पन्न होइत छैक ।

मानवता ऐन्हऽ युग म॑ प्रवेश करी गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ ओकरऽ इंजीनियरिंग क्षमता असाधारण होय गेलऽ छै, लेकिन प्राकृतिक खतरा क॑ बढ़ाबै के क्षमता भी असाधारण होय गेलऽ छै । एहि तरहें मानवता लेल अपन सुरक्षित संचालन स्थान कए बुझब अनिवार्य अछि ।

प्रकृति माता के सम्मान के मतलब विकास के त्याग या इंजीनियरिंग के अस्वीकार करब नै छै। एकरऽ मतलब छै कि ई बात क॑ स्वीकार करना कि मानवीय चातुर्य क॑ प्राकृतिक प्रक्रिया के खिलाफ नै बल्कि ओकरऽ साथ काम करना चाहियऽ ।

टिकाऊ मार्ग प्रकृति के महारत नै, संचालन छै। एकरा म॑ नदी क॑ अंतहीन रूप स॑ संकुचित करै के बजाय बाढ़ के मैदानऽ के सुरक्षा, पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र क॑ सरल बनाबै के बजाय जैव विविधता के संरक्षण, आरू प्राकृतिक प्रवाह क॑ पुनर्इंजीनियरिंग के बजाय ओकरा समायोजित करै वाला बुनियादी ढाँचा के डिजाइन करना शामिल छै ।

हम प्रकृति के मानवीय महत्वाकांक्षा आ लोभ के प्रति मोड़य के कोशिश करैत रहि सकैत छी, या प्रकृति के डिजाइन के भीतर रहब सीख सकैत छी. हिमालय अपन फैसला स्पष्ट रूप स देलक अछि।

ब्रह्मा चेलानी नौ पुस्तक के लेखक छै, जेकरा म॑ पुरस्कृत “ पानी: एशिया केरऽ नया युद्ध के मैदान ।“ शामिल छै ।

title: West Hartford’s Nepalese Community Gathers to Honor Nepal Flood Victims - We-Ha
description: West Hartford’s Nepalese Community Gathers to Honor Nepal Flood Victims  We-Ha
publisher.title: We-Ha
full_article:
When a candle is lit in Nepalese culture, it can serve two purposes: to illuminate the path for those who have died and, during Diwali, to help those far from home find their way back.

By Mia Jaworski

“Tonight, we need both,” said Rupesh Parajuli, chief adviser to the Nepalese Association of Connecticut, during a candlelight vigil Sunday evening on the steps outside of West Hartford Town Hall.

Candlelight vigil for Nepal flood victims at West Hartford Town Hall on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

About 100 people gathered for the vigil, organized by the Nepalese Association of Connecticut, a registered 501(c)(3) organization serving Connecticut’s Nepali community, that has its headquarters in West Hartford.

The gathering honored those killed or still missing after a devastating flash flood swept through villages in a Himalayan valley along the Nepal-Tibet border.

#gallery-1 { margin: auto; } #gallery-1 .gallery-item { float: left; margin-top: 10px; text-align: center; width: 33%; } #gallery-1 img { border: 2px solid #cfcfcf; } #gallery-1 .gallery-caption { margin-left: 0; } /* see gallery_shortcode() in wp-includes/media.php */

Damaged homes are filled with mud and debris in Devighat on Saturday. Rajesh Kumar Singh/AP Mud covers a building in Nuwakot on August 26, 2026. Safal Prakash Shrestha/Anadolu/Getty Images/CNN This aerial photo, taken on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026 shows mud covering buildings in Trishuli. Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters/CNN



At least 1,287 people are known to have died and more than 5,000 remain missing nearly two weeks after the disaster, according to figures cited by the BBC.

The flooding, believed to have been triggered by a glacial collapse, sent a massive surge of water, ice, mud, and rocks through the Lhende Khola river valley on Aug. 26. Rivers rose by an estimated 15 to 20 meters, burying villages, roads, bridges and thousands of people.

Candlelight vigil for Nepal flood victims at West Hartford Town Hall on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

For Connecticut’s Nepalese community, the disaster was not distant.

According to a 2020 Connecticut Asian Pacific Islander Ethnicities map produced by UConn’s Asian American Studies Institute and the CTData Center, about 2,099 Nepalese people live in Connecticut, including 999 in Hartford County.

West Hartford is home to the state’s largest Nepalese population, and annually celebrates Nepal Day in town.

West Hartford resident and Community Engagement Librarian Pramod Pradhan, in a 2024 CT Insider article, said families have been drawn to the town by its schools, public safety, libraries and proximity to the Nepalese community. He estimated that about 100 homes in West Hartford were owned by Nepalese residents, many in the Elmwood neighborhood.

Sunday’s vigil began with the greeting “Namaste,” followed by the national anthems of Nepal and the United States.

Candlelight vigil for Nepal flood victims at West Hartford Town Hall on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

Parajuli addressed the crowd gathered at the bottom of the Town Hall steps, leaving space for a large tribute arranged on the ground. A Nepalese flag was surrounded by tea-light candles forming a heart and the word “pray.”

Candlelight vigil for Nepal flood victims at West Hartford Town Hall on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

“This is what we have – each other,” Parajuli told the crowd.

Connecticut state Rep. Kate Farrar, who represents the 20th District, followed with remarks of support for the Nepalese community.

“We want all the Nepalese in West Hartford and across Connecticut to know that we stand with you and we want to support you as friends and in any way we can financially,” Farrar said.

West Hartford Town Council members John Lyons, Tiffani McGinnis, Barry Walters, Jason Wang, and Ben Wenograd also addressed the gathering. They emphasized that the disaster was not only a catastrophe overseas but one that deeply affected people in their own community.

West Hartford Town Council members Ben Wenograd, Barry Walters, Tiffani McGinnis, John Lyons and Jason Wang, from left, attend a candlelight vigil for victims of the Nepal floods on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

“It’s not only heartbreaking, but deeply personal,” McGinnis said.

Parajuli’s father-in-law, who arrived from Nepal last week, also spoke in Nepali about witnessing the devastation firsthand and seeing the destruction caused by the floods.

Rupesh Parajuli’s father-in-law speaks to the crowd about witnessing the devastation from the disaster firsthand in Nepal at candlelight vigil on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

As the vigil continued, attendees moved around the tribute, lighting candles, praying and embracing one another.

Candlelight vigil for Nepal flood victims at West Hartford Town Hall on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

Candlelight vigil for Nepal flood victims at West Hartford Town Hall on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

The ceremony ended with a moment of silence for those who died and those who remain missing.

Throughout the service, speakers urged attendees to contribute to disaster relief efforts. Donations to the Nepal Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund can be made through the fund’s online donation portal.

Donation box at candlelight vigil for Nepal flood victims at West Hartford Town Hall on Sept. 6, 2026. Photo credit: Mia Jaworski

नेपाली संस्कृति मे जखन मोमबत्ती जराओल जाइत अछि त दू टा काज भ सकैत अछि : जे मरि गेल छथि हुनका लेल बाट रोशन करब आ दिवाली के दौरान घर सं दूर लोक के वापसी के रास्ता खोजय मे मदद करब.

मिया जावोर्स्की द्वारा

वेस्ट हार्टफोर्ड टाउन हॉल के बाहर सीढ़ी पर रविदिन साँझ मे मोमबत्ती के रोशनी में जागरण के दौरान नेपाली एसोसिएशन ऑफ कनेक्टिकट के मुख्य सलाहकार रूपेश पराजुली कहलनि जे, आइ राति हमरा सब के दुनू के जरूरत अछि।

वेस्ट हार्टफोर्ड टाउन हॉल मे नेपाल के बाढ़ि पीड़ित के लेल मोमबत्ती के रोशनी मे जागरण 6 सितम्बर 2026. फोटो क्रेडिट: मिया जावोर्स्की

title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster - theguardian.com
description: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster  theguardian.com
publisher.title: theguardian.com
full_article:
Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.

Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.

A journey to the frontline of Nepal’s disastrous floods – podcast Read more

Speaking to the Guardian, Nepal’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, was forthright in his call for climate justice and said it was imperative the world’s biggest economies stepped up to help Nepal recover and rebuild after the catastrophic floods.

Nepal contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, while its neighbours India and China are among the world’s biggest emitters. The mountains of the Himalayas – which span across India, China, Nepal and Bhutan – have been warming at a rate nearly 50% faster than the global average.

In 2023, the UN said Nepal’s mountains had lost close to a third of their ice in just over 30 years due to global heating.

Khanal emphasised that the recent disaster was far more extreme than any flooding regularly seen during the monsoon season, and said the magnitude of damage was on par with the 2015 earthquake that left much of the country in ruins.

View image in fullscreen An excavator repairs a damaged road in Nepal near the Trishuli River on Monday. Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

“This felt like a tsunami that was coming from the Himalayas,” he said. “We experienced waves as high as 60, 70 feet, which were mixed with debris, mud, stones, rocks, and came at the speed of almost 180km per hour. Towns, villages and highways were completely wiped out and there are some areas still disconnected.”

Khanal confirmed that Nepal’s ministry of finance and ministry of environment had written a joint letter to the UN’s fund for responding to loss and damage – which was set up in 2022 in line with the Paris climate agreement – to request $20m in climate-related damages.

“We have contributed so little to climate change,” he said. “It is imperative for those in the global community who benefit from larger, much more polluting economies, and whose historical contribution to greenhouse gases is much bigger than ours, to accept a shared responsibility. This affects all of humanity.”

For Nepal, the disaster was particularly worrying because it was “one of the strongest warning signals that we’ve experienced of what’s to come”, he said.

“The global community should not see this as one-off disaster; it should be viewed in the context of the changing climate in the Himalayas,” he said. “We know it is going to be a recurring scenario that more and more communities, not just in Nepal but around the world, will have to face.”

Khanal acknowledged that the compensation amount Nepal has requested from the UN was “obviously not nearly enough to cover the damage that we have sustained”. According to some estimates, the total damage caused by the floods will be upwards of $5bn, though Khanal said it could be even higher.

Upwards of 20,000 homes will probably have to be rebuilt, as well as the main highway. Villages built in vulnerable areas along the river, some of which washed away entirely, may have to be relocated to higher, safer ground.

While Khanal initially singled out India and China as countries that should step in to help – while avoiding mention of the US, which is the world’s biggest polluter – he rowed back on those comments, saying: “It is not just about shifting the blame to one or the other country, it’s about us all working together.”

View image in fullscreen Damaged buildings on the banks of the Trishuli River. Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

He emphasised that the compensation demand was also meant to act as a “wake-up call for the global community to establish a more robust mechanism to help vulnerable and small economies like Nepal”.

After the flood: human suffering on an unfathomable scale in Nepal’s worst-hit districts Read more

The UN has admitted the loss and damage fund is already facing a “significant financing gap”. The fund has already received requests totalling $2.8bn from about 119 countries, but so far only around $400m has been given by the international community. The US has given just $17m, after Donald Trump withdrew from the Paris agreement.

Khanal acknowledged there were “political challenges” in getting Nepal the climate compensation it was demanding.

“Yes there always will be people who may not agree to our perspective or deny there is climate change, but there are also people who deny that the Earth is round,” he said bluntly.

He emphasised the importance of funds being made available not just for immediate disaster response but also for preparedness and mitigation for climate-related risk.

Khanal rebuffed allegations that China had failed to give an adequate warning or share data with Nepal about the impending floods. He said he was in discussion with China about enhancing coordination and data sharing for the Himalayan region.

“With the benefit of hindsight, we can now see that this glacier was fragile and had been receding in the past six months,” he said.

“But before the floods hit, there was no knowledge on our part, or on the part of Chinese scientists, that this particular collapse was imminent. I do not believe any of us had any idea of the threat until it happened.”
